Fax: +81 197 68 3881.cite13†Search for more papers by this author L139: \\nL140: First published: 03 December 2014\\nL141: \\nL142: cite16†https://doi.org/10.1016/j.febslet.2014.11.045Digital Object Identifier (DOI)†doi.org L143: \\nL144: view metrics\\nL145: \\nL146: Sections\\nL147: \\nL148: CITE\\nL149: \\nL150: cite17†Tools L151: \\nL152: Share full-text access\\nL153: Please review our cite18†Terms and Conditions of Use†onlinelibrary.wiley.com and check box below to share full-text version of article.\\nL154: \\nL155: [Input]I have read and accept the Wiley Online Library Terms and Conditions of Use\\nL156: \\nL157: * * *\\nL158: \\nL159: Shareable Link\\nL160: \\nL161: Use the link below to share a full-text version of this article with your friends and colleagues. cite19†Learn more.†onlinelibrary.wiley.com L162: \\nL163: [Button: Copy URL]\\nL164: \\nL165: Share a link\\nL166: \\nL167: Share on\\nL168: ## Abstract\\nL169: The major flavonoids accumulated in leaves of Japanese gentian (Gentiana triflora) were determined as isoorientin (luteolin 6-C-glucoside) and isoorientin 4′-glucoside. A cDNA (GtUF6CGT1) was isolated that encoded the UDP-glucose-dependent glucosyltransferase that is involved in C-glycosylflavone biosynthesis. The recombinant GtUF6CGT1 protein could transfer a glucose group to the C6 position of a flavone skeleton through C-linkage, using UDP-glucose as the glucosyl donor.\\nL170: These C-glycosylflavones also accumulated in petals. A good correlation was observed between GtUF6CGT1 expression and C-glycosylflavone accumulation in leaves and petals. GtUF6CGT1 is the first reported C-glucosyltransferase that mediates direct C-glucosylation of the flavone skeleton.\\nL171: ## 1 Introduction\\nL172: Flavonoids are a major class of plant secondary metabolites that are commonly accumulated in the vacuole as their glycosides, with some exceptions [cite20†1 ]. Flavone, a major class of flavonoids, is commonly conjugated with a sugar group through an O-glycosidic linkage. Some flavones exist as the C-glycosylated form and are often modified with O- and C-glycosylations. C-glycosylflavones are an important subgroup of flavonoids present in many plants [cite20†1 ].\\nL173: C-glycosylflavones are involved in UV protection, defense against pathogens and inhibition of caterpillar growth [cite21†2 ]. C-glycosylflavones are also co-pigments for flower coloration, antioxidants and anti-diabetic compounds [cite22†3 ]. Flavonoid O-glycosides are commonly generated by the glycosylation of the flavone skeleton, mediated by uridine diphosphate (UDP)-sugar-dependent glycosyltransferase (UGT) [cite23†4 ]. The biosynthetic pathway of C-glycosylflavone was determined recently [cite23†4 ].\\nL174: In 2009, Brazier-Hicks et al. first identified C-glucosyltransferases (CGTs) involved in the biosynthesis of C-glycosylflavone in rice (Oryza sativa). C-glycosylflavone is synthesized via glucosylation of the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone produced by the hydroxylation of flavanone mediated by a cytochrome P450 family protein, followed by enzymatic dehydration (cite24†Fig. 1 , Route 1) [cite25†5 , cite26†6 ].\\nL175: Thus, in cereals, C-glycosylflavones are generated by C-glycosylation before the flavone skeleton is complete. The same pathway exists in buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum) [cite27†7 ].\\nL176: Fig. 1\\nL177: \\nL178: cite17†Open in figure viewer cite28†PowerPoint L179: \\nL180: The possible biosynthetic pathways for C-glycosylflavone. The pathways of C-glycosylflavone synthesis have been proposed as: Route 1, glycosylation occurs at the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone in rice and maize. Route 2 illustrates the other possible pathway for C-glycosylflavone in Japanese gentian.\\nL181: Japanese-cultivated gentians, Gentiana triflora, Gentiana scabra and their hybrids, are popular ornamental flowers in Japan. They typically show blue to violet flower color, but some pink- or white-colored cultivars have been bred [cite29†8 -cite30†10 ]. These cyanic flower colors arise from polyacylated anthocyanins and the structures of those compounds were determined as gentiodelphin [cite31†11 , cite32†12 ].\\nL182: Besides anthocyanins, Japanese-cultivated gentians accumulate unpigmented flavonoids, including flavone derivatives. Previously, we isolated the flavone synthase II (FNSII) gene, which is involved in flavone biosynthesis in gentian petals [cite33†13 ]. Recently, we characterized the transcription factors involved in the activation and repression of flavonoid biosynthetic genes in Japanese gentians [cite34†14 , cite35†15 ].\\nL183: However, the molecular structures of these flavonoids have not been determined and no enzymatic genes involved in flavone modification have been isolated.\\nL184: In this report, we attempted to determine the structures of flavones accumulated in Japanese gentian and to identify a cDNA encoding the UDP-glucose-dependent glucosyltransferase. The results showed that C-glycosylflavones accumulate in the leaves and petals of Japanese gentian. A cDNA, GtUF6CGT1, encoding a protein involved in the formation of flavone 6-C-glucosides was identified.\\nL185: In vitro assays using flavonoids as substrates demonstrated that the recombinant GtUF6CGT1 protein could transfer a glucose moiety to the 6 position of the flavone skeleton with a C-linkage. GtUF6CGT1 could catalyze direct C-glucosylation to the flavone skeleton with high stereo selectivity, which differs from previously reported CGTs.\\nL186: ## 2 Materials and methods\\nL187: ### 2.1 Plant materials and chemicals\\nL188: Japanese-cultivated gentian (G. triflora) cv. Maciry was grown in the field of the Iwate Agricultural Research Center. The petals at developmental stages 1–4, as described in our previous report [cite36†16 ], young and mature leaves, and stems were collected and immediately frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C. 2-Hydroxynaringenin and norathyriol were purchased from ChemFaces (Wuhan, China). Maclurin was purchased from Sigma (St. Louis, MO, USA).\\nL189: Other flavonoids were purchased from Funakoshi (Tokyo, Japan).\\nL190: ### 2.2 Purification of flavonoids extracted from gentian leaves\\nL191: Freeze-dried leaves (20 g, dry weight) were soaked in 80% methanol. The filtered extract was evaporated and dissolved in pure water. Flavonoids were absorbed to a Diaion HP20 column (Mitsubishi Chemical, Tokyo, Japan) equilibrated with pure water. Flavonoids were eluted with 50% methanol after washing with 20% methanol.\\nL192: Flavonoids were separated using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC; L-6250 Intelligent Pump, L-4250 UV–VIS detector, D-2500 Chromato-Integrator, Hitachi High-Technologies, Tokyo, Japan) equipped with a reverse-phase column (Inertsil ODS, 10 i.d. × 250 mm, GL Science, Tokyo, Japan). The first separation used a linear gradient elution (2 ml min^{−1}) of 5–60% methanol in 0.1% aqueous trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) for 40 min.\\nL193: Fractions were analyzed by an HPLC-PDA (HPLC-photodiode array detector; AS-4010 Auto sampler, L-6320 Intelligent pump, L-2455 Diode Array Detector, D-2000 Elite chromatography DATA station, Hitachi High-Technologies) at 1-min intervals and the fractions containing flavonoids were combined and subjected to the second purification step. The second cycle of HPLC separation used a linear gradient elution (2 ml min^{−1}) of 5–45% acetonitrile in 0.1% aqueous TFA for 40 min.\\nL194: The fraction containing compound 1 was subjected to flash chromatography (YFLC AI-580, Yamazen Corp., Osaka, Japan) equipped with a doubled reverse-phase column (Hi-Flash column, ODS-SM, 26 i.d. × 100 mm, Yamazen) using a linear gradient elution (10 ml min^{–1}) of 10–80% methanol in water for 40 min.\\nL195: Purified flavonoids were analyzed by electrospray ionization-mass spectrometry (ESI-MS, AccuTOF MS, JMS-T100LC, JEOL Ltd., Tokyo, Japan) and nuclear magnetic resonance (^{1}H NMR, ^{13}C NMR, ^{1}H{^{13}C} HMQC, ^{1}H{^{13}C} HMBC, ^{1}H-^{1}H COSY, and NOESY) in CD_{3}SOCD_{3} on a JNM-ECA-500 spectrometer (JEOL). For ^{1}H NMR (500 MHz) and ^{13}C NMR (125 MHz), chemical shifts were referenced to the residual solvent (CD_{3}SOCD_{3}) signals at δ_{H} 2.50 and δ_{C} 39.5.\\nL196: The assignments of NMR signals are shown in cite37†Table S1 . Purified compound 1 was hydrolyzed by treatment with 4 N HCl at 80 °C. The hydrolysate was labeled with p-aminobenzoic acid ethylester (ABEE) following the manufacturer's protocol (ABEE labeling kit, J-oil mills, Tokyo, Japan). Labeled sugars were separated by HPLC on a reverse-phase column (COSMOSIL5C18-MS-II, 4.6 mm i.d.\\nL197: × 50 mm) using isocratic elution (1.5 ml min^{−1}) of 0.2 M potassium borate buffer (pH 8.9), including 7% acetonitrile, for 5 min. The sugars were identified by comparing their retention times with standard hexoses (glucose and galactose).\\nL198: ### 2.3 C-glucosylation assay using the crude protein prepared from gentian young leaf\\nL199: Frozen leaves (0.5 g) were ground into powder in liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle and then placed into 5 ml of extraction buffer (0.1 M potassium phosphate, pH 7.5, containing 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT)). Cell debris was removed by centrifugation at 15 000×g for 5 min. Proteins were precipitated with 80% ammonium sulfate and re-suspended in extraction buffer. Crude protein was desalted using a G-25 spin column (GE Healthcare, Piscataway, NJ, USA).\\nL200: The reaction mixture comprised 100 mM Tris–Cl buffer, pH 8.5, 1 mM DTT, 0.2 mM of substrate and 40–60 μg of crude protein. A CBB protein assay kit (BioRad Laboratories, Hercules, CA, USA) determined the protein concentrations, using bovine serum albumin as the standard.\\nL201: ### 2.4 Cloning CGT candidate cDNAs and the production of recombinant proteins\\nL202: UGT homologous cDNAs were searched for using our in-house expressed sequence tag (EST) database [cite34†14 ]. Six cDNA sequences containing putative ATG start codons were selected and PCR primers were designed to include the first ATG (cite37†Supple. Table S2 ). Total RNA was extracted from young leaves using an RNeasy Plant Mini kit (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany) following the manufacturer's manual.\\nL203: First strand cDNA was synthesized by rapid amplification of cDNA ends (RACE), using a 3′-RACE core kit (TakaraBio, Shiga, Japan). The 3′-cDNA ends from the first ATG obtained by PCR (20 s at 95 °C, 40 s at 55 °C, 1 min at 72 °C, 35 cycles) were ligated into vector pMD20 (TakaraBio) and sequenced. Each cDNA containing an open reading frame was amplified by PCR under the same conditions using sense primers including first ATG and an antisense primer designed to exclude the stop codon (cite37†Supple.\\nL204: Table S2 ) and ligated into vector pTrcHis2/TOPO (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA). Escherichia coli Nico21 (DE3) were transformed with these plasmids. Four hundred microliters of pre-inoculated (1.5 ml LB-broth, 16 h at 30 °C) transformants were transferred to 200 ml of LB-broth, and inoculated for 16 h at 30 °C. After IPTG (1 mM final concentration) addition for protein induction, the cells were incubated for 14 h at 16 °C. Harvested E. coli cells were stored at −20 °C. The E.\\nL205: coli cells were suspended in extraction buffer (0.1 M potassium phosphate, pH 7.5, 0.5 M NaCl, 20 mM imidazole) and disrupted by sonication. After centrifugation of 15 000×g for 2 min at 4 °C, the supernatant was applied to a HisTrap GraviFlow column equilibrated with extraction buffer.\\nL206: The column was washed with 3 mL of wash buffer (0.1 M potassium phosphate, pH 7.5, 0.5 M NaCl, 50 mM imidazole) three times; the proteins were eluted with elution buffer (0.1 M potassium phosphate, pH 7.5, 0.5 M NaCl, 250 mM imidazole). The concentration and buffer exchange to 10 mM potassium phosphate buffer (pH 7.5) including 1 mM DTT was done using an Amicon-15 (30 MWCO, Merck Millipore, Darmstadt, Germany).\\nL207: ### 2.5 C-glucosylation assay using the partially purified recombinant GtUFCGT\\nL208: \\nL209: The reaction mixture comprised 100 mM Tris–Cl buffer, pH 8.5, 1 mM DTT, 0.2 mM of substrate and 16 μg of partially purified recombinant protein. The mixtures were preincubated at 30 °C, and then enzyme reaction was started by the addition of UDP-glucose. Two μl of 20% phosphoric acid was added to terminate the reaction after 10 min.\\nL210: ### 2.6 Determination of the compounds generated using recombinant GtUF6CGT1\\nL211: A large amount of reaction product was obtained by the UDP-glucose recycling system using Arabidopsis sucrose synthase [cite38†17 ], following the protocol described in the literature [cite39†18 ]. The reaction mixture was separated by HPLC as described above, using a linear gradient elution (2 ml min^{−1}) of 5–60% methanol in 0.1% aqueous TFA for 40 min and fractionated by 1 min. The purified reaction products were analyzed by MS and NMR. The NMR assignment of reaction products is shown in cite37†Table S1 .\\nL212: ### 2.7 Quantification of the C-glycosylflavone content\\nL213: \\nL214: Flavonoids contained in each tissue (10 mg dry weight) were extracted with 1 ml of 80% methanol containing 0.1% TFA overnight. The supernatants were treated with 4 N HCl for 2 h at 80 °C. After cooling on ice, four volumes of methanol were added to the mixture. The hydrolyzed samples were evaporated, dissolved in methanol and then subjected to HPLC analysis.\\nL215: ### 2.8 Expression analysis of GtUF6CGT1\\nL216: \\nL217: Quantitative real-time reverse-transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) analysis was performed as described previously [cite35†15 ], using the primers described in cite37†Supple. Table S2 . The expression level of GtUF6CGT1 was normalized by the expression of the ubiquitin gene [cite35†15 ]. The individual expression levels were shown in cite37†Supple. Fig. S1 .\\nL218: ### 2.9 Phylogenetic analysis\\nL219: \\nL220: The amino acid sequences were aligned using the ClustalW algorithm [cite40†19 ]. The phylogenetic tree was constructed using the neighbor-joining algorithm in MEGA version 5.2.2 [cite41†20 ]. Bootstrap values were performed with 1000 replications.\\nL221: \\nL222: ## 3 Results\\nL223: ### 3.1 Flavonoid analysis of the gentian leaves\\nL224: In the gentian leaf extract, two major peaks were detected on the HPLC chromatogram with a λmax at 338 nm (cite42†Fig. 2 peak 1) and at 350 nm (cite42†Fig. 2 peak 2), suggesting that they could be flavone derivatives. The two substances corresponding to peaks 1 and 2 were purified by HPLC.\\nL225: The molecular ion peaks of the compounds were observed [M+H]^{+} at m/z 471.15 (peak 2) and [M+Na]^{+} at m/z 611.21 (peak 1) suggesting luteolin C-hexoside and luteolin C-hexoside bonding to additional hexose through an O-linkage, respectively.\\nL226: The retention time of peak 2 corresponded to that of isoorientin (luteolin 6-C-glucoside) and the heteronuclear multiple-bond correlation spectroscopy (HMBC) correlation signal was observed between the anomeric proton of glucose and C-6 indicated that this compound was isoorientin (cite37†Supple. Fig. S2 ). HPLC analysis of labeled hydrolyzed hexose of compound 1 strongly suggested that the hexose was glucose (cite37†Supple. Fig. S3 ).\\nL227: The nuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy (NOESY) signal between the anomeric proton of O-linked glucose and the proton at the 5′ position suggested that glucose was linked at the 4′ position (cite37†Supple. Fig. S4 ). The MS analysis implied that the minor peak (cite42†Fig. 2 asterisk; the molecular ion peak was observed [M+Na]^{+} at m/z = 617.11) is apigenin C-hexoside-O-hexoside.\\nL228: Fig. 2\\nL229: \\nL230: cite17†Open in figure viewer cite43†PowerPoint L231: \\nL232: HPLC elution profile of the extracts from gentian leaves. The extracts from Japanese gentian leaves were separated by HPLC monitoring at 350 nm. Two major peaks were observed on the chromatogram. These two major compounds were identified as isoorientin and isoorientin 4′-glucoside (see the text).\\nL233: ### 3.2 Detection of the flavone glucosyltransferase activity using crude protein from gentian leaves\\nL234: After incubation of the crude protein prepared from young leaves with the UDP-glucose as the glucose donor and luteolin as the glucose acceptor for 30 min, the reaction products were subjected to HPLC analysis. No significant product peaks were observed in the reaction mixture lacking UDP-glucose (cite44†Fig. 3 A). An additional peak was observed on the HPLC chromatogram in the mixture containing UDP-glucose (cite44†Fig. 3 B).\\nL235: HPLC co-chromatography demonstrated that the retention time of the product corresponded to that of isoorientin (cite44†Fig. 3 D). These data suggested that the reaction whereby the glucose group was directly bonded to the flavone through a C-linkage was mediated by a UDP-glucose-dependent enzyme in the mixture.\\nL236: Fig. 3\\nL237: \\nL238: cite17†Open in figure viewer cite45†PowerPoint L239: HPLC analysis of the enzymatic reaction products. The product of the glucosylation reaction using the crude protein prepared from gentian leaf excluding UDP-glucose in the mixture (A), and UDP-glucose including in the mixture (B). Flavone standards (C) and co-chromatography B and C (D). The product of glucosylation reaction using the partially purified recombinant protein excluding UDP-glucose in the mixture (E), and including UDP-glucose in the mixture (F).\\nL240: ### 3.3 Isolation of the cDNA encoding UF6CGT\\nL241: BLAST searching against our in-house EST database [cite34†14 ] identified 70 UGT-like cDNA fragments. Twenty-five of them containing a putative ATG start codon were selected as the candidate of UF6CGT. Finally, six cDNAs containing a full-length open reading frame were obtained by 3′-RACE. Recombinant expressions constructs of these six cDNAs were introduced to E. coli cells. The UGT activity assay showed that one cDNA clone, designated as GtUF6CGT1 (accession No.\\nL242: AB985754), could transfer a glucosyl group to luteolin. HPLC analysis of the enzymatic reaction products obtained using the crude recombinant protein showed a reaction product when UDP-glucose was present, but not when UDP-glucose was absent (cite44†Fig. 3 E and F). MS analysis showed that the molecular ion peak at m/z = 471.15 ([M+Na]^{+}) corresponded to the molecular mass of isoorientin. The chemical shift of ^{1}H and ^{13}C NMR values also corresponded to those from gentian leaf extracts (cite37†Supple.\\nL243: Table S1 ). The observation of the HMBC signals between the anomeric proton of glucose and carbon at the 6 position suggested that the compound was luteolin 6-C-glucoside (cite37†Supple. Fig. S2 ). The coupling constant of the anomeric proton suggested that luteolin binds to glucose via β-conjugation.\\nL244: ### 3.4 Gene expression analysis of GtUF6CGT1 and C-glycosylflavone contents in leaves and flower petals\\nL245: The C-glycosylflavone content was measured in each tissue. C-glycosylflavones accumulated at the highest level in young leaves (cite46†Fig. 4 A). Accumulation was also observed in mature leaves and in each developmental stage of the petals. qRT-PCR analysis revealed that GtUF6CGT1 expression was highest in young leaves and reduced in mature leaves (cite46†Fig. 4 B). The amino acid sequence shared low identities with rice (25%) and maize (25%) CGTs that mediate the C-glucosylation of ring opened 2-hydroxyflavanone. The fact that GtUF6CGT1 belongs to the clade that include Arabidopsis UGT84 family implied GtUF6CGT1 was categorized in group L of family 1 UDP-glycosyltransferases proposed by Li et al. [cite48†21 ].\\nL254: Phylogenetic tree analysis based on the deduced amino acid sequences suggested that the GtUF6CGT1 is close to UGTs involved in acyl-glucose biosynthesis and but not to CGTs in cereals. Fig. S5 ).\\nL255: ### 3.6 Substrate preference of the recombinant GtUF6CGT1\\nL256: The substrate preference of GtUF6CGT1 was assessed using the partially purified recombinant protein (cite49†Table 1 ). Fax: +81 197 68 3881.cite13†Search for more papers by this author L139: \\nL140: First published: 03 December 2014\\nL141: \\nL142: cite16†https://doi.org/10.1016/j.febslet.2014.11.045Digital Object Identifier (DOI)†doi.org L143: \\nL144: view metrics\\nL145: \\nL146: Sections\\nL147: \\nL148: CITE\\nL149: \\nL150: cite17†Tools L151: \\nL152: Share full-text access\\nL153: Please review our cite18†Terms and Conditions of Use†onlinelibrary.wiley.com and check box below to share full-text version of article.\\nL154: \\nL155: [Input]I have read and accept the Wiley Online Library Terms and Conditions of Use\\nL156: \\nL157: * * *\\nL158: \\nL159: Shareable Link\\nL160: \\nL161: Use the link below to share a full-text version of this article with your friends and colleagues. cite19†Learn more.†onlinelibrary.wiley.com L162: \\nL163: [Button: Copy URL]\\nL164: \\nL165: Share a link\\nL166: \\nL167: Share on\\nL168: ## Abstract\\nL169: The major flavonoids accumulated in leaves of Japanese gentian (Gentiana triflora) were determined as isoorientin (luteolin 6-C-glucoside) and isoorientin 4′-glucoside. A cDNA (GtUF6CGT1) was isolated that encoded the UDP-glucose-dependent glucosyltransferase that is involved in C-glycosylflavone biosynthesis. The recombinant GtUF6CGT1 protein could transfer a glucose group to the C6 position of a flavone skeleton through C-linkage, using UDP-glucose as the glucosyl donor.\\nL170: These C-glycosylflavones also accumulated in petals. A good correlation was observed between GtUF6CGT1 expression and C-glycosylflavone accumulation in leaves and petals. GtUF6CGT1 is the first reported C-glucosyltransferase that mediates direct C-glucosylation of the flavone skeleton.\\nL171: ## 1 Introduction\\nL172: Flavonoids are a major class of plant secondary metabolites that are commonly accumulated in the vacuole as their glycosides, with some exceptions [cite20†1 ]. Flavone, a major class of flavonoids, is commonly conjugated with a sugar group through an O-glycosidic linkage. Some flavones exist as the C-glycosylated form and are often modified with O- and C-glycosylations. C-glycosylflavones are an important subgroup of flavonoids present in many plants [cite20†1 ].\\nL173: C-glycosylflavones are involved in UV protection, defense against pathogens and inhibition of caterpillar growth [cite21†2 ]. C-glycosylflavones are also co-pigments for flower coloration, antioxidants and anti-diabetic compounds [cite22†3 ]. Flavonoid O-glycosides are commonly generated by the glycosylation of the flavone skeleton, mediated by uridine diphosphate (UDP)-sugar-dependent glycosyltransferase (UGT) [cite23†4 ]. The biosynthetic pathway of C-glycosylflavone was determined recently [cite23†4 ].\\nL174: In 2009, Brazier-Hicks et al. first identified C-glucosyltransferases (CGTs) involved in the biosynthesis of C-glycosylflavone in rice (Oryza sativa). C-glycosylflavone is synthesized via glucosylation of the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone produced by the hydroxylation of flavanone mediated by a cytochrome P450 family protein, followed by enzymatic dehydration (cite24†Fig. 1 , Route 1) [cite25†5 , cite26†6 ].\\nL175: Thus, in cereals, C-glycosylflavones are generated by C-glycosylation before the flavone skeleton is complete. The same pathway exists in buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum) [cite27†7 ].\\nL176: Fig. 1\\nL177: \\nL178: cite17†Open in figure viewer cite28†PowerPoint L179: \\nL180: The possible biosynthetic pathways for C-glycosylflavone. The pathways of C-glycosylflavone synthesis have been proposed as: Route 1, glycosylation occurs at the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone in rice and maize. Route 2 illustrates the other possible pathway for C-glycosylflavone in Japanese gentian.\\nL181: Japanese-cultivated gentians, Gentiana triflora, Gentiana scabra and their hybrids, are popular ornamental flowers in Japan. They typically show blue to violet flower color, but some pink- or white-colored cultivars have been bred [cite29†8 -cite30†10 ]. These cyanic flower colors arise from polyacylated anthocyanins and the structures of those compounds were determined as gentiodelphin [cite31†11 , cite32†12 ].\\nL182: Besides anthocyanins, Japanese-cultivated gentians accumulate unpigmented flavonoids, including flavone derivatives. Previously, we isolated the flavone synthase II (FNSII) gene, which is involved in flavone biosynthesis in gentian petals [cite33†13 ]. Recently, we characterized the transcription factors involved in the activation and repression of flavonoid biosynthetic genes in Japanese gentians [cite34†14 , cite35†15 ].\\nL183: However, the molecular structures of these flavonoids have not been determined and no enzymatic genes involved in flavone modification have been isolated.\\nL184: In this report, we attempted to determine the structures of flavones accumulated in Japanese gentian and to identify a cDNA encoding the UDP-glucose-dependent glucosyltransferase. The results showed that C-glycosylflavones accumulate in the leaves and petals of Japanese gentian. A cDNA, GtUF6CGT1, encoding a protein involved in the formation of flavone 6-C-glucosides was identified.\\nL185: In vitro assays using flavonoids as substrates demonstrated that the recombinant GtUF6CGT1 protein could transfer a glucose moiety to the 6 position of the flavone skeleton with a C-linkage. GtUF6CGT1 could catalyze direct C-glucosylation to the flavone skeleton with high stereo selectivity, which differs from previously reported CGTs.\\nL186: ## 2 Materials and methods\\nL187: ### 2.1 Plant materials and chemicals\\nL188: Japanese-cultivated gentian (G. triflora) cv. Maciry was grown in the field of the Iwate Agricultural Research Center. The petals at developmental stages 1–4, as described in our previous report [cite36†16 ], young and mature leaves, and stems were collected and immediately frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C. 2-Hydroxynaringenin and norathyriol were purchased from ChemFaces (Wuhan, China). Maclurin was purchased from Sigma (St. Louis, MO, USA).\\nL189: Other flavonoids were purchased from Funakoshi (Tokyo, Japan).\\nL190: ### 2.2 Purification of flavonoids extracted from gentian leaves\\nL191: Freeze-dried leaves (20 g, dry weight) were soaked in 80% methanol. The filtered extract was evaporated and dissolved in pure water. Flavonoids were absorbed to a Diaion HP20 column (Mitsubishi Chemical, Tokyo, Japan) equilibrated with pure water. Flavonoids were eluted with 50% methanol after washing with 20% methanol.\\nL192: Flavonoids were separated using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC; L-6250 Intelligent Pump, L-4250 UV–VIS detector, D-2500 Chromato-Integrator, Hitachi High-Technologies, Tokyo, Japan) equipped with a reverse-phase column (Inertsil ODS, 10 i.d. × 250 mm, GL Science, Tokyo, Japan). The first separation used a linear gradient elution (2 ml min^{−1}) of 5–60% methanol in 0.1% aqueous trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) for 40 min.\\nL193: Fractions were analyzed by an HPLC-PDA (HPLC-photodiode array detector; AS-4010 Auto sampler, L-6320 Intelligent pump, L-2455 Diode Array Detector, D-2000 Elite chromatography DATA station, Hitachi High-Technologies) at 1-min intervals and the fractions containing flavonoids were combined and subjected to the second purification step. The second cycle of HPLC separation used a linear gradient elution (2 ml min^{−1}) of 5–45% acetonitrile in 0.1% aqueous TFA for 40 min.\\nL194: The fraction containing compound 1 was subjected to flash chromatography (YFLC AI-580, Yamazen Corp., Osaka, Japan) equipped with a doubled reverse-phase column (Hi-Flash column, ODS-SM, 26 i.d. × 100 mm, Yamazen) using a linear gradient elution (10 ml min^{–1}) of 10–80% methanol in water for 40 min.\\nL195: Purified flavonoids were analyzed by electrospray ionization-mass spectrometry (ESI-MS, AccuTOF MS, JMS-T100LC, JEOL Ltd., Tokyo, Japan) and nuclear magnetic resonance (^{1}H NMR, ^{13}C NMR, ^{1}H{^{13}C} HMQC, ^{1}H{^{13}C} HMBC, ^{1}H-^{1}H COSY, and NOESY) in CD_{3}SOCD_{3} on a JNM-ECA-500 spectrometer (JEOL). For ^{1}H NMR (500 MHz) and ^{13}C NMR (125 MHz), chemical shifts were referenced to the residual solvent (CD_{3}SOCD_{3}) signals at δ_{H} 2.50 and δ_{C} 39.5.\\n\"}"+'\n') p=O/'phase_io.py';s=p.read_text().replace('"https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/"','"https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/","https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/"');write('TASK-017-PREP',str(p),s) plan=json.loads((O/'citation_followup_plan.json').read_text());plan['maximum_HTTP_followups']=6;plan['primary_publisher_free_access_page_verified']=True;write('TASK-017-PREP',str(O/'citation_followup_plan.json'),json.dumps(plan,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)+'\n') ns={};exec(compile(s,str(p),'exec'),ns) url='https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1016/j.febslet.2014.11.045' row=ns['fetch'](url,O/'articles/Sasaki2015/main.pdf','cited_primary_article_PDF',33554432) print(json.dumps(row,ensure_ascii=False),flush=True)

A cDNA (GtUF6CGT1) was isolated that encoded the UDP-glucose-dependent glucosyltransferase that is involved in C-glycosylflavone biosynthesis. The recombinant GtUF6CGT1 protein could transfer a glucose group to the C6 position of a flavone skeleton through C-linkage, using UDP-glucose as the glucosyl donor.\\nL170: These C-glycosylflavones also accumulated in petals. A good correlation was observed between GtUF6CGT1 expression and C-glycosylflavone accumulation in leaves and petals. GtUF6CGT1 is the first reported C-glucosyltransferase that mediates direct C-glucosylation of the flavone skeleton.\\nL171: ## 1 Introduction\\nL172: Flavonoids are a major class of plant secondary metabolites that are commonly accumulated in the vacuole as their glycosides, with some exceptions [cite20†1 ]. Flavone, a major class of flavonoids, is commonly conjugated with a sugar group through an O-glycosidic linkage. Some flavones exist as the C-glycosylated form and are often modified with O- and C-glycosylations. C-glycosylflavones are an important subgroup of flavonoids present in many plants [cite20†1 ].\\nL173: C-glycosylflavones are involved in UV protection, defense against pathogens and inhibition of caterpillar growth [cite21†2 ]. C-glycosylflavones are also co-pigments for flower coloration, antioxidants and anti-diabetic compounds [cite22†3 ]. Flavonoid O-glycosides are commonly generated by the glycosylation of the flavone skeleton, mediated by uridine diphosphate (UDP)-sugar-dependent glycosyltransferase (UGT) [cite23†4 ]. The biosynthetic pathway of C-glycosylflavone was determined recently [cite23†4 ].\\nL174: In 2009, Brazier-Hicks et al. first identified C-glucosyltransferases (CGTs) involved in the biosynthesis of C-glycosylflavone in rice (Oryza sativa). C-glycosylflavone is synthesized via glucosylation of the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone produced by the hydroxylation of flavanone mediated by a cytochrome P450 family protein, followed by enzymatic dehydration (cite24†Fig. 1 , Route 1) [cite25†5 , cite26†6 ].\\nL175: Thus, in cereals, C-glycosylflavones are generated by C-glycosylation before the flavone skeleton is complete. The same pathway exists in buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum) [cite27†7 ].\\nL176: Fig. 1\\nL177: \\nL178: cite17†Open in figure viewer cite28†PowerPoint L179: \\nL180: The possible biosynthetic pathways for C-glycosylflavone. The pathways of C-glycosylflavone synthesis have been proposed as: Route 1, glycosylation occurs at the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone in rice and maize. Route 2 illustrates the other possible pathway for C-glycosylflavone in Japanese gentian.\\nL181: Japanese-cultivated gentians, Gentiana triflora, Gentiana scabra and their hybrids, are popular ornamental flowers in Japan. They typically show blue to violet flower color, but some pink- or white-colored cultivars have been bred [cite29†8 -cite30†10 ]. These cyanic flower colors arise from polyacylated anthocyanins and the structures of those compounds were determined as gentiodelphin [cite31†11 , cite32†12 ].\\nL182: Besides anthocyanins, Japanese-cultivated gentians accumulate unpigmented flavonoids, including flavone derivatives. Previously, we isolated the flavone synthase II (FNSII) gene, which is involved in flavone biosynthesis in gentian petals [cite33†13 ]. Recently, we characterized the transcription factors involved in the activation and repression of flavonoid biosynthetic genes in Japanese gentians [cite34†14 , cite35†15 ].\\nL183: However, the molecular structures of these flavonoids have not been determined and no enzymatic genes involved in flavone modification have been isolated.\\nL184: In this report, we attempted to determine the structures of flavones accumulated in Japanese gentian and to identify a cDNA encoding the UDP-glucose-dependent glucosyltransferase. The results showed that C-glycosylflavones accumulate in the leaves and petals of Japanese gentian. A cDNA, GtUF6CGT1, encoding a protein involved in the formation of flavone 6-C-glucosides was identified.\\nL185: In vitro assays using flavonoids as substrates demonstrated that the recombinant GtUF6CGT1 protein could transfer a glucose moiety to the 6 position of the flavone skeleton with a C-linkage. GtUF6CGT1 could catalyze direct C-glucosylation to the flavone skeleton with high stereo selectivity, which differs from previously reported CGTs.\\nL186: ## 2 Materials and methods\\nL187: ### 2.1 Plant materials and chemicals\\nL188: Japanese-cultivated gentian (G. triflora) cv. Maciry was grown in the field of the Iwate Agricultural Research Center. The petals at developmental stages 1–4, as described in our previous report [cite36†16 ], young and mature leaves, and stems were collected and immediately frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C. 2-Hydroxynaringenin and norathyriol were purchased from ChemFaces (Wuhan, China). Maclurin was purchased from Sigma (St. Louis, MO, USA).\\nL189: Other flavonoids were purchased from Funakoshi (Tokyo, Japan).\\nL190: ### 2.2 Purification of flavonoids extracted from gentian leaves\\nL191: Freeze-dried leaves (20 g, dry weight) were soaked in 80% methanol. The filtered extract was evaporated and dissolved in pure water. Flavonoids were absorbed to a Diaion HP20 column (Mitsubishi Chemical, Tokyo, Japan) equilibrated with pure water. Flavonoids were eluted with 50% methanol after washing with 20% methanol.\\nL192: Flavonoids were separated using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC; L-6250 Intelligent Pump, L-4250 UV–VIS detector, D-2500 Chromato-Integrator, Hitachi High-Technologies, Tokyo, Japan) equipped with a reverse-phase column (Inertsil ODS, 10 i.d. × 250 mm, GL Science, Tokyo, Japan). The first separation used a linear gradient elution (2 ml min^{−1}) of 5–60% methanol in 0.1% aqueous trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) for 40 min.\\nL193: Fractions were analyzed by an HPLC-PDA (HPLC-photodiode array detector; AS-4010 Auto sampler, L-6320 Intelligent pump, L-2455 Diode Array Detector, D-2000 Elite chromatography DATA station, Hitachi High-Technologies) at 1-min intervals and the fractions containing flavonoids were combined and subjected to the second purification step. The second cycle of HPLC separation used a linear gradient elution (2 ml min^{−1}) of 5–45% acetonitrile in 0.1% aqueous TFA for 40 min.\\nL194: The fraction containing compound 1 was subjected to flash chromatography (YFLC AI-580, Yamazen Corp., Osaka, Japan) equipped with a doubled reverse-phase column (Hi-Flash column, ODS-SM, 26 i.d. × 100 mm, Yamazen) using a linear gradient elution (10 ml min^{–1}) of 10–80% methanol in water for 40 min.\\nL195: Purified flavonoids were analyzed by electrospray ionization-mass spectrometry (ESI-MS, AccuTOF MS, JMS-T100LC, JEOL Ltd., Tokyo, Japan) and nuclear magnetic resonance (^{1}H NMR, ^{13}C NMR, ^{1}H{^{13}C} HMQC, ^{1}H{^{13}C} HMBC, ^{1}H-^{1}H COSY, and NOESY) in CD_{3}SOCD_{3} on a JNM-ECA-500 spectrometer (JEOL). For ^{1}H NMR (500 MHz) and ^{13}C NMR (125 MHz), chemical shifts were referenced to the residual solvent (CD_{3}SOCD_{3}) signals at δ_{H} 2.50 and δ_{C} 39.5.\\nL196: The assignments of NMR signals are shown in cite37†Table S1 . Purified compound 1 was hydrolyzed by treatment with 4 N HCl at 80 °C. The hydrolysate was labeled with p-aminobenzoic acid ethylester (ABEE) following the manufacturer's protocol (ABEE labeling kit, J-oil mills, Tokyo, Japan). Labeled sugars were separated by HPLC on a reverse-phase column (COSMOSIL5C18-MS-II, 4.6 mm i.d.\\nL197: × 50 mm) using isocratic elution (1.5 ml min^{−1}) of 0.2 M potassium borate buffer (pH 8.9), including 7% acetonitrile, for 5 min. Cell debris was removed by centrifugation at 15 000×g for 5 min. Proteins were precipitated with 80% ammonium sulfate and re-suspended in extraction buffer. Crude protein was desalted using a G-25 spin column (GE Healthcare, Piscataway, NJ, USA).\\nL200: The reaction mixture comprised 100 mM Tris–Cl buffer, pH 8.5, 1 mM DTT, 0.2 mM of substrate and 40–60 μg of crude protein. A CBB protein assay kit (BioRad Laboratories, Hercules, CA, USA) determined the protein concentrations, using bovine serum albumin as the standard.\\nL201: ### 2.4 Cloning CGT candidate cDNAs and the production of recombinant proteins\\nL202: UGT homologous cDNAs were searched for using our in-house expressed sequence tag (EST) database [cite34†14 ]. Six cDNA sequences containing putative ATG start codons were selected and PCR primers were designed to include the first ATG (cite37†Supple. Table S2 ). Total RNA was extracted from young leaves using an RNeasy Plant Mini kit (QIAGEN, Hilden, Germany) following the manufacturer's manual.\\nL203: First strand cDNA was synthesized by rapid amplification of cDNA ends (RACE), using a 3′-RACE core kit (TakaraBio, Shiga, Japan). Each cDNA containing an open reading frame was amplified by PCR under the same conditions using sense primers including first ATG and an antisense primer designed to exclude the stop codon (cite37†Supple.\\nL204: Table S2 ) and ligated into vector pTrcHis2/TOPO (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA). Escherichia coli Nico21 (DE3) were transformed with these plasmids. After IPTG (1 mM final concentration) addition for protein induction, the cells were incubated for 14 h at 16 °C. Harvested E. coli cells were stored at −20 °C. After centrifugation of 15 000×g for 2 min at 4 °C, the supernatant was applied to a HisTrap GraviFlow column equilibrated with extraction buffer.\\nL206: The column was washed with 3 mL of wash buffer (0.1 M potassium phosphate, pH 7.5, 0.5 M NaCl, 50 mM imidazole) three times; the proteins were eluted with elution buffer (0.1 M potassium phosphate, pH 7.5, 0.5 M NaCl, 250 mM imidazole). Two μl of 20% phosphoric acid was added to terminate the reaction after 10 min.\\nL210: ### 2.6 Determination of the compounds generated using recombinant GtUF6CGT1\\nL211: A large amount of reaction product was obtained by the UDP-glucose recycling system using Arabidopsis sucrose synthase [cite38†17 ], following the protocol described in the literature [cite39†18 ]. Fax: +81 197 68 3881.cite13†Search for more papers by this author L139: \\nL140: First published: 03 December 2014\\nL141: \\nL142: cite16†https://doi.org/10.1016/j.febslet.2014.11.045Digital Object Identifier (DOI)†doi.org L143: \\nL144: view metrics\\nL145: \\nL146: Sections\\nL147: \\nL148: CITE\\nL149: \\nL150: cite17†Tools L151: \\nL152: Share full-text access\\nL153: Please review our cite18†Terms and Conditions of Use†onlinelibrary.wiley.com and check box below to share full-text version of article.\\nL154: \\nL155: [Input]I have read and accept the Wiley Online Library Terms and Conditions of Use\\nL156: \\nL157: * * *\\nL158: \\nL159: Shareable Link\\nL160: \\nL161: Use the link below to share a full-text version of this article with your friends and colleagues. cite19†Learn more.†onlinelibrary.wiley.com L162: \\nL163: [Button: Copy URL]\\nL164: \\nL165: Share a link\\nL166: \\nL167: Share on\\nL168: ## Abstract\\nL169: The major flavonoids accumulated in leaves of Japanese gentian (Gentiana triflora) were determined as isoorientin (luteolin 6-C-glucoside) and isoorientin 4′-glucoside. A cDNA (GtUF6CGT1) was isolated that encoded the UDP-glucose-dependent glucosyltransferase that is involved in C-glycosylflavone biosynthesis. The recombinant GtUF6CGT1 protein could transfer a glucose group to the C6 position of a flavone skeleton through C-linkage, using UDP-glucose as the glucosyl donor.\\nL170: These C-glycosylflavones also accumulated in petals. A good correlation was observed between GtUF6CGT1 expression and C-glycosylflavone accumulation in leaves and petals. GtUF6CGT1 is the first reported C-glucosyltransferase that mediates direct C-glucosylation of the flavone skeleton.\\nL171: ## 1 Introduction\\nL172: Flavonoids are a major class of plant secondary metabolites that are commonly accumulated in the vacuole as their glycosides, with some exceptions [cite20†1 ]. Flavone, a major class of flavonoids, is commonly conjugated with a sugar group through an O-glycosidic linkage. Some flavones exist as the C-glycosylated form and are often modified with O- and C-glycosylations. C-glycosylflavones are an important subgroup of flavonoids present in many plants [cite20†1 ].\\nL173: C-glycosylflavones are involved in UV protection, defense against pathogens and inhibition of caterpillar growth [cite21†2 ]. C-glycosylflavones are also co-pigments for flower coloration, antioxidants and anti-diabetic compounds [cite22†3 ]. Flavonoid O-glycosides are commonly generated by the glycosylation of the flavone skeleton, mediated by uridine diphosphate (UDP)-sugar-dependent glycosyltransferase (UGT) [cite23†4 ]. The biosynthetic pathway of C-glycosylflavone was determined recently [cite23†4 ].\\nL174: In 2009, Brazier-Hicks et al. first identified C-glucosyltransferases (CGTs) involved in the biosynthesis of C-glycosylflavone in rice (Oryza sativa). C-glycosylflavone is synthesized via glucosylation of the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone produced by the hydroxylation of flavanone mediated by a cytochrome P450 family protein, followed by enzymatic dehydration (cite24†Fig. 1 , Route 1) [cite25†5 , cite26†6 ].\\nL175: Thus, in cereals, C-glycosylflavones are generated by C-glycosylation before the flavone skeleton is complete. The same pathway exists in buckwheat (Fagopyrum esculentum) [cite27†7 ].\\nL176: Fig. 1\\nL177: \\nL178: cite17†Open in figure viewer cite28†PowerPoint L179: \\nL180: The possible biosynthetic pathways for C-glycosylflavone. The pathways of C-glycosylflavone synthesis have been proposed as: Route 1, glycosylation occurs at the open-chain form of 2-hydroxyflavanone in rice and maize. Route 2 illustrates the other possible pathway for C-glycosylflavone in Japanese gentian.\\nL181: Japanese-cultivated gentians, Gentiana triflora, Gentiana scabra and their hybrids, are popular ornamental flowers in Japan. They typically show blue to violet flower color, but some pink- or white-colored cultivars have been bred [cite29†8 -cite30†10 ]. These cyanic flower colors arise from polyacylated anthocyanins and the structures of those compounds were determined as gentiodelphin [cite31†11 , cite32†12 ].\\nL182: Besides anthocyanins, Japanese-cultivated gentians accumulate unpigmented flavonoids, including flavone derivatives. Previously, we isolated the flavone synthase II (FNSII) gene, which is involved in flavone biosynthesis in gentian petals [cite33†13 ]. U1 用户明确：浙江大学、化学系；真实实验数据和合作实验室待定。不假定其职称、具体课程或已有产业合同。

P1 用户通知与高校转发：未来健康包括合成生物；10/13–11/20申报及接口测试，11/21推荐，11/23开放。

## 文献事实
L1 Pei et al.2019 DOI 10.1007/s10600-019-02712-9：糖基转移酶与蔗糖合酶协同制异槲皮苷，当前仅核到出版摘要。
L2 Zhang et al.2015 DOI 10.1007/s10529-015-1792-6 / PMID25724715：芦丁酶转化为异槲皮苷的原始研究。
L3 Niu et al.2024 DOI 10.1186/s12934-024-02390-5：枯草芽孢杆菌糖供体与降解通路工程，可支撑特定底盘扰动案例；不是从葡萄糖全合成。
L4 Nature Communications2025 DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-61530-6：高通量糖基转移酶底物筛查支持AI排序场景，不能自动作定量产率真值。
## 模型与术语
逆合成搜索产生候选；前向仿真按经审定模型产生结果；大模型负责解释/工具编排；这三者不同。文献复现、经验模型、概念示意、实验观测需可见标记。
## 禁止主张
无临床疗效或食品/药品批准推定；不把工程测试当科学验证；不把历史曝光当fresh；不虚构合作/课程/学生/试教成效；无细胞酶法不冒称底盘设计。

课程、负责人资格、学校名额与校内期限、真实实验场景归属、文献图数据可用性、资产托管许可、平台部署与等保覆盖、接口密钥和实际验收均未落实。

## 已知、未知及冲突

能否在不虚构科学/教学成效的前提下，利用既有底座交付有真实实验支撑、可操作评价且可共享的未来健康虚拟实验？

有条件可行；首选健康相关黄酮糖苷生物制造，以酶法合成/供体循环为化学核心，并配一个经过数据审定的底盘扰动案例；不能直接改名上传。

**有条件可行，值得推进，但当前版本不能直接改名上传。** FlavoRetro 已经拥有真实 AI 搜索、黄酮糖苷结构与反应证据、可追溯运行和网页工作台。它最有价值的转换是：把“研究者寻找候选路线”转成“学生提出方案、审查 AI、执行有依据的虚拟实验、分析结果并修正设计”。

主推荐题名：

**AI赋能健康相关黄酮糖苷的酶法合成与生物制造虚拟仿真实验**

推荐归属为“未来健康—合成生物相关实验教学”，具体以健康相关天然产物的制造问题、酶催化与糖供体工程为对象。题名保留化学系的结构、选择性、物料衡算和分析化学优势；不直接承诺完整底盘细胞自动设计、药效预测或发酵数字孪生。

最小建设范围建议为“一个主目标、两类教学模块、一条完整实验闭环”：

- 主目标：优先论证异槲皮苷，最终由化学与生物催化教师审定身份、来源、条件和数据。
- 模块A：围绕酶法合成/选择性转化，比较糖基化、供体再生和去糖路线，完成投料、对照、取样、定量与结果解释。
- 模块B：用同一目标的已报道工程菌案例，让学生选择有证据的底盘与供体/降解通路方案，比较相应真实数据，解释“表达了酶却未高产”的原因。
- AI贯穿实验前、中、后：方案提示与证据检索、过程诊断、实验后反思；数值结果由独立仿真/数据服务给出，评分由规则和教师量规定稿。

**本轮能否申报，首先取决于三件事：校内推荐与课程资格、真实实验场景及案例数据、可承载公开服务并有适用安全证明的平台。** AI接口开发本身并非最难的一项。

若模块B只能做论文浏览，报告与申报中应称“底盘工程案例分析”，不能写成完整“底盘细胞设计”。若仅有纯逆合成和无细胞酶反应，也不能自行认定已充分符合未来健康的合成生物口径，应请校内组织审核方向契合。未来制造中的生物制造可作为方向口径不被认可时的备选，但不能为此随意更换科学内容。

### 3.2 需要优先补建的能力

第一层缺口是“实验”。目前没有学生实验状态机、虚拟投料/取样/分析操作、经过审定的前向反馈模型、独立教学答案和评分。只在搜索框旁添加聊天窗口，仍然不能完成这层转换。

第二层缺口是“教学运行”。当前web.py使用全局BoundedSemaphore(1)，搜索同步执行，忙时返回429；没有学生、班级、教师角色与逐用户运行权限。运行历史按工作区公开，/api/status返回内部STATE和服务器路径。教学门户应与研究管理界面建立权限边界，敏感状态和全工作区历史不应对公共访问者开放。现有前端提交参数也未带领域库开关/版本，不能把后端拥有糖苷模块写成已向学生开放。

第三层缺口是“可持续公开服务”。排队、任务隔离、超时、资源配额、备份、浏览器与网络验证、学校安全证明和外部平台回传都要补齐。父服务与worker的旧领域版本接线还存在静态一致性疑点，须在后续授权建设中回归；本轮未复现，不作为已确认运行缺陷。

### 3.3 科学状态如何影响申报

STATE明确：方法与有限开发交付已完成，正式C/SS独立迁移未验证，TASK-017相关科研准入未通过，科学效果保持null；历史停止与曝光记录保留。

这不等于“不能开展教学建设”。教学版可以限定在教师审定、来源与适用范围清楚的案例，检验学生能否正确设计和分析实验；它不必先证明一个通用逆合成方法对所有黄酮泛化。但应建立独立的教学案例审核与教学验收，不能修改研究门槛或把历史卡片换名变成独立gold。

建议保存三套分开的状态：research_evaluation、teaching_case_review、public_teaching_release。教学公开上线不自动改变前两者；已有科研资产也不自动取得公开教学许可。

## 四、与你的专业及浙大条件的结合

已确认的背景是“浙江大学化学系”和围绕FlavoRetro的黄酮/糖苷结构、反应证据、逆合成软件工作。可以据此设计以下分工，不能进一步推定你的职称、已授课程、论文、实验室资源或产业关系。

化学系应主导目标分子身份、立体与区域选择性、酶法/化学法比较、物料衡算、分析鉴定及证据边界。这些构成项目的学科主体。生物催化或合成生物教师补足酶、宿主、供体代谢、竞争通路和真实实验场景。技术人员负责服务、学习状态、AI适配和iLab；不由软件人员独自裁定酶活与实验答案。

与已有项目背景的融合应体现方法，而不是把全部项目拼接进去：

- FlavoRetro提供结构、路线、搜索与证据追溯。
- 既有条件数据治理经验可帮助设计单位、零/缺失、重复、条件比较与适用范围；CondRxnBench并非现成酶催化预测器，其数据、许可和任务适配不能默认跨项目复用。
- 文献整理经验可支撑教师案例包与来源定位；论文摘要不能直接代替原始定量数据或独立答案。

浙江大学已有虚拟仿真实验共享平台，也公开介绍过合成生物学实验课程。可优先向校内平台确认托管、身份接入、测评适用关系及运行支持，并邀请相应领域教师参与；本文没有联系任何人，也未落实合作。[浙大共享平台](https://ilab.zju.edu.cn/)、[合成生物学课程](https://zjubiolab.zju.edu.cn/page/course/detail/154/2359)

学校AI STEP介绍了虚拟实验建设以及“智海”“浙大先生”等资源，可以作为校内模型服务路线的调研线索，不能假定已有API权限或免费额度。该页面URL含2026，但正文记载的发布事件为2025年3月，本文不把它误写为2026新政策。[浙大AI STEP介绍](https://ai.zju.edu.cn/2026/0112/c89504a3127572/page.htm)

## 六、科学场景：为什么优先论证异槲皮苷

候选主目标为异槲皮苷，即槲皮素-3-O-β-D-葡萄糖苷。它与不同位点的槲皮素糖苷、芦丁、酶改性异槲皮苷EMIQ应严格区分，不可仅按名称合并。

外部原始研究提供三个互相关联、又必须分开的教学场景：

|场景|原始研究能支持的内容|模型与教学边界|
|---|---|---|
|槲皮素酶促加糖与供体再生|Pei等2019研究UGT与蔗糖合酶耦合制备异槲皮苷|本轮核到公开摘要，完整条件/原始数据仍需取得与核对|
|芦丁选择性去鼠李糖|Zhang等2015研究重组α-L-rhamnosidase转化，含动力学线索|这是水解，不是UGT糖基化；参数不跨酶/体系迁移|
|工程菌将外加槲皮素转化为产物|Niu等2024研究B.subtilis糖供体、底物降解和产物水解工程|不是从葡萄糖全合成，也不是本校已验证生产工艺|

[Pei等2019](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10600-019-02712-9)、[Zhang等2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25724715/)、[Niu等2024](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12934-024-02390-5)

它们共享目标，适合教授“同一产物可以有不同制造路径”；不能据此共享同一响应面、动力学参数或真值。Niu研究中的供体工程并未单独解决产物积累问题，适合训练学生考察竞争代谢与降解；不要设计“每改一个基因产量就增加固定比例”的游戏规则。

酶候选排序可以作为后续AI方向。Yang等2018的活性预测研究与2025年的GT高通量谱说明该问题有实验数据基础；后者初筛与选定纯酶复核存在差异，数据也不适合直接比较不同底物的催化效率。它们支持“AI建议需要实验核对”，不支持把大规模筛查结果直接转为高可信产率模拟器或全部位点真值。[Yang等2018](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41589-018-0154-9)、[GT高通量原始研究2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-61530-6)

健康关联应表述为“健康相关天然产物研究与制造场景”。合成路线、体外性质、工艺产率不推出临床疗效、给药建议、食品可用性或药品上市资格。教学不需要承担临床决策任务。

## 七、把科研工具变成一次完整虚拟实验

### 7.1 教学对象与学习目标

建议优先面向已学有机化学、分析化学与基础生物化学的高年级本科生，依托综合化学实验、化学生物学或相关课程中的一个实验单元。具体课程名称、学分、教学计划与授课资格须由化学系确定，本文不虚构已纳入课程。

建议4学时，暂按每学时45分钟共180分钟设计，按学校安排调整。完成后应能：

- 正确识别母核、连接位点、糖型及反应方向，区分加糖与去糖。
- 比较自主方案与AI建议，指出证据、范围和缺口。
- 设计对照、投料、取样和定量方案，完成物料衡算。
- 基于观测解释供体、降解与选择性问题，并提出一次有依据的修正。
- 识别模型不可支持的条件，不把AI排序当作成功概率。

这五项是拟实现的学习目标，不是已测到的能力提升。

### 7.2 24步实质性交互方案

每步均要求学生提交选择、数值或理由并获得反馈。登录、加载、浏览下一页、纯视频观看不计步数；实际教学脚本还需教师审定。

|步骤|学生动作|可观察反馈或产物|
|---|---|---|
|01|从结构中确认目标产物并标注糖连接位点|结构与位点校验|
|02|区分芦丁、异槲皮苷和位置异构糖苷|身份差异及错误解释|
|03|判断两条候选反应属于加糖还是去糖|反应方向与键变化|
|04|给来源卡分级，选出能够支持本案例的证据|证据等级与缺口|
|05|独立选择初始路线并提交理由|保存未经AI提示的方案|
|06|登记可检验假设和预期失败原因|假设与观测变量匹配检查|
|07|调用AI/搜索获取限定候选并进行排序|真实调用结果及来源|
|08|拒绝一条超范围建议并说明依据|守卫、证据和拒绝理由反馈|
|09|选择经过审定的酶/反应体系|身份、底物范围和限制|
|10|选择糖供体与再生方案，或解释水解无需该供体|路径特异的物料约束|
|11|设置空白、无酶或对应阴性对照|对照能否识别替代解释|
|12|输入底物、体积与单位并计算投料|单位、摩尔量与守恒检查|
|13|选择数据支持的缓冲/溶剂与pH条件|范围支持或明确拒绝|
|14|选择已测/已标定的温度和酶量档位|适用域及资源消耗|
|15|设计单变量比较，保留基线条件|可比性与混杂检查|
|16|设置取样时点并确认定量方案|采样计划合理性反馈|
|17|执行基线虚拟实验，观察对照和实验组|有来源标签的实验结果|
|18|辨认目标、底物和未知峰，选择积分区间|分析身份/积分错误反馈|
|19|依据标准曲线、稀释倍数计算浓度|可重放的数值检查|
|20|计算转化率、产物收率和选择性并检查衡算|底物消失是否等于产物生成|
|21|为底盘模块选定有证据的宿主与工程方案|显示方案适用性及可用对照|
|22|比较对应工程菌数据，判断供体/降解限制|真实数据差异与未支持解释|
|23|在预算内修改一次方案并运行有支持的比较|第一次与修正结果并列|
|24|提交证据约束的结论、未解问题及下一实验设计|量规反馈与教师复核入口|

模块A为步骤01—20的主实验；模块B为21—22的最低衔接，并在23—24体现方案迭代。若没有可用底盘数据，21—22不能用宣传图替代，应调整教学脚本并重新审核方向契合及实质步数。模块A中的去糖路线可先作为路线对照，不必同时建设两套完整连续动力学模拟器。

学生选择未测的底盘组合时，可保存为研究假设，系统返回“无对应实验数据，不能给定量结果”，并引导设计验证；不能补造预测值来保持流程流畅。

### 7.3 四学时安排与赋分

|学时|主要任务|过程与结果分值|
|---|---|---|
|1|结构、身份、证据，步骤01—06|结构与证据20分|
|2|AI比较、酶/供体、对照及投料，步骤07—12|路线与理由20分|
|3|条件、采样、执行及定量，步骤13—20|实验设计20分、计算分析20分|
|4|底盘比较、一次迭代、解释与独立小测，步骤21—24|迭代与边界20分|

数值题依据固定公式、单位与版本化容差评分；开放题按明确量规，由教师定稿。AI可提供反馈草稿，不单独决定最终成绩。记录提示使用次数用于分析学习过程，不简单按“少用AI=高分”惩罚基础不同的学生。提供统一提示权限、申诉及教师复核，检验不同学习基础群体的评分公平性。

能力画像只记录有证据的结构判断、证据审查、设计、定量、反思五个维度及变化，不能据有限行为贴心理或天赋标签。最优产率不是唯一正确答案；合理识别模型不足也应得分。

## 八、真实实验数据与前向仿真的可行路径

### 8.1 目前“待定”的三个层面

外部论文确实包含真实实验；尚未确定本项目可使用哪些原始/授权数据；本校的课程、实验场景归属、合作教师及补充测定还未落实。这三个层面不同，不能笼统写“没有任何真实数据”，也不能把外部论文变成本校成果。

优先顺序建议：有授权的校内/合作实验数据；可合法教学复用的开放原始数据；经授权和核对的文献图表数字化。摘要终点产率和自行画出的曲线不能支撑定量实验仿真。数字化图数据应标注提取方法和误差，保留原位置，并由教师审核其教学用途。

### 8.2 教学数据包最低内容

每个案例需独立登记目标与底物完整结构、反应方向、酶/宿主身份、糖供体及条件域；投料、体积、单位、取样时点、对照与重复；标准品与标准曲线、色谱或其他可复核分析记录；失败、零、缺失和未知峰；原始数据位置、授权、版本与审核人。

教师审定记录必须显示实际审核者与日期。Cano整理和机器核验只能标agent_delegated，不能预填human_reviewed。原有受限反应库和资料包不整体公开，只使用逐项已准入的教学子集。

### 8.3 仿真按证据选择，不能先承诺连续预测

|等级|实现方式|适用条件|允许输出|
|---|---|---|---|
|D1|真实实验条件的离散查询/重放|有对应条件与可复核数据|明确标记“来源实验数据”|
|D2|有界插值或经验模型|覆盖网格、独立验证和误差足够|标明插值/估计及支持区间|
|D3|经标定机理模型|有足够初速、时序、重复和独立条件|模型预测、参数来源和误差|
|D4|概念演示|无足够定量依据|仅机制示意，不作为定量实验结果或成绩真值|

最现实的申报版以D1为基础，D2/D3在数据允许时增加；离散查询也必须反映真实科学规律，支持学生控制、对照、取样与分析，不能退化成固定答案播放。其能否达到征集“真仿真”要求应由校内学术审核，单有二十次点击不构成达标。

纯酶水解可从单底物Michaelis–Menten起步：dS/dt = −Vmax·S/(Km+S)，但Vmax、酶量、单位、底物范围和失活必须与该酶、体系匹配。不能仅凭论文一个终点唯一确定模型。UGT与供体再生体系应分别处理双底物、UDP与供体循环；没有参数时使用已测离散条件。

底盘模块初期优先使用已有工程组合的真实对照数据；不把基因改动线性叠加。不建设未经验证的连续生长、发酵、传质模型，也不在缺数据时声称数字孪生。所有范围外输入均返回“不支持定量预测”，保存学生假设并提示后续验证。

## 九、AI方向转换与接口架构

### 9.1 四种职责分开

|层次|职责|建议近期实现|验证方法|
|---|---|---|---|
|化学工具/搜索|结构校验、候选路线、证据和范围|复用受控现有模块，教学案例版本冻结|案例合同及结构/范围核验|
|仿真/数据服务|给出受条件控制的实验观测|D1优先，D2/D3有依据才用|守恒、单位、对照、重放与误差|
|大模型导师|解释、追问、检索和工具编排|基于审定案例的检索增强与工具调用|引文存在、越界拒绝、错误挑战集|
|学习/评价服务|状态、步骤、成绩、反馈及iLab|确定性计算与教师量规|重放一致、权限隔离、回传核对|

推荐数据流为“学习者门户 → 教学会话/权限 → AI导师及受控工具 → 仿真与案例数据 → 评分/档案 → iLab适配器”。研究管理接口留在内部，教学运行使用单独命名空间和存储权限。

### 9.2 “AI接口”具体应做什么

模型调用应由后端统一代理，支持校内服务或学校批准的外部服务；模型名称、版本、部署类型、证据快照和提示模板版本记录到会话。不把服务密钥写进网页或学生端。

适合首版的工具包括validate_structure、retrieve_case_evidence、search_candidate_routes、check_experiment_design、run_supported_simulation、calculate_material_balance。它们是拟议内部能力名，不是平台已经提供的API。工具仅接受结构化、经过校验的参数，不提供任意shell、文件读写或访问研究库权限。

导师在实验前帮助发现缺对照和证据；实验中检查单位与异常，提醒“底物下降不等于目标增加”；实验后引导比较假设与观测。结果引用对应case_id、dataset_hash和实验条件。没有证据时明确未知，不补引文、酶活、产率或谱图。

对学生不必展示所有哈希和实现字段，保留可点击的来源、模型/数据类型、适用范围和限制；完整技术指纹供教师和审核使用。

### 9.3 拟议内部教学API

以下为设计建议，尚未实现，路径与字段可在后续任务中细化：

|接口|用途|关键约束|
|---|---|---|
|POST /teaching/sessions|创建经授权的实验会话|用户、课程、案例版本绑定|
|POST /teaching/sessions/{id}/steps|记录学生动作|序号、时间、参数、理由、重复次数|
|POST /teaching/ai/assist|导师提示与证据检索|权限/配额、工具白名单、使用统计|
|POST /teaching/simulations|提交支持域内实验|案例数据域验证；异步返回job_id|
|GET /teaching/jobs/{id}|获取结果与排队状态|只允许所有者或授权教师访问|
|POST /teaching/sessions/{id}/finalize|冻结报告与最终分数|教师量规版本、完整步骤与审计|
|内部iLab上传作业|回传结果/AI统计/报告|服务端凭据、重试与完成冻结|

优先复用研究服务作为内部工具，不让大模型自由指定模型资产或任意版本。教学案例固定领域库与配置，避免普通学生选到未验收的历史版本。

### 9.4 中期AI研究可以如何增长

首版不自训基础大模型。等教学案例积累后，可分别申请有界研究任务：酶/底物候选排序、条件优化建议、实验失败诊断。每项都需要可用标签、明确任务和来源分组留出；不能用学生交互或历史曝光数据立即宣称独立泛化。

可把“预测失败与不确定性”设计为学习任务：AI高排名候选未必有实验支持，学生应发现并提出验证。这样复用现有项目的证据优势，而不是用新大模型遮盖旧证据缺口。

## 十、实验空间2026接口：已经核到哪些内容

官方说明明确：2026年沿用2022接口，新增AI应用过程统计ai_data。无需猜一套新标准；也不能只接普通聊天接口就称完成国家平台对接。[2026接口说明](https://shenbao.ilab-x.com/declare/wiki/v2#1-3)、[官方动态正文](https://shenbao.ilab-x.com/js/wiki_v2.js)

接入流程为：用户在实验空间登录并携ticket跳转实验URL；后端以平台appid及secret按规范换取用户信息和access_token；执行并保存实验；向结果接口提交步骤、分数和AI数据；有实验报告时按规定后续上传。

已核实的生产接口包括https://www.ilab-x.com/open/api/v2/token与https://www.ilab-x.com/open/api/v2/data_upload。token请求含ticket、appid、signature；签名按官方规定使用解码ticket与APPID、SECRET计算MD5并转大写，拼URL时再按规范编码。凭据只在服务端处理，敏感query不进入普通访问日志；有效期及刷新依平台返回和最新规范处理。本次没有申请密钥或实际调用这些业务接口。

### 10.1 官方ai_data字段

|字段|必需|规则|
|---|---|---|
|ai_call_count|是|非负整数，记录真实AI调用次数|
|ai_models_used|是|数组；调用为0可空，大于0不得空|
|ai_usage_scenarios|是|数组；调用大于0不得空且元素不得空|
|ai_input_token_count|否|提交时为非负整数|
|ai_output_token_count|否|提交时为非负整数|
|ai_remark|否|字符串|

模型数组每项必有model、version、deployment，provider可选；deployment枚举为公有云服务、私有化部署、混合服务、本地运行。ai_data及模型元素不能添加未定义字段；相关校验失败返回码19。对2026推荐项目完成记录status=1校验，未完成status=2暂不按该条件校验。

校内应确定“调用”的计数口径：至少将实际导师模型请求与已用模型如实记录，内部另存工具、搜索和错误事件；MCTS内部每一步不能未经定义就当一次大模型调用。非语言模型没有token概念时不伪造token，选填字段按实际能观测的数据提交；最终映射需与平台联调确认。

协议允许一次记录AI调用为0，只是表达和容错规则，不等于项目不需要大模型赋能。不能用接口返回成功代替教学质量审查。

### 10.2 实验过程与结果

原有结果包含username、title、status、score、startTime、endTime、timeUsed、appid、originId、steps；每步含序号、名称、起止时间、实际/合理用时、满分/得分、重复次数、评价和赋分模型。时间戳按规范为13位，用时以秒计。科学参数和来源指针优先内部保存，并按ext_data的允许结构扩展；不要放进禁止额外字段的ai_data。

用同一稳定originId关联本次实验。未完成记录按规范更新，完成后不再修改；最终上传前应复核成绩。超时重试须识别重复记录和既有回执，不能每重试一次创建一条新实验；依照实际错误码管理状态和token刷新。

必须先测试环境、再正式密钥与地址联通。正式自查要求至少3个真实用户、10条真实有效的虚拟实验运行记录，结果与用时应有差异。它不是10份湿实验数据，也不证明教学效果。

**两个步数门槛必须分开：接口完成记录仍按不少于10步校验；本次申报设计要求不少于20步实质性交互。** 本方案按24步设计，并应在实测中核查其真实性。平台已联通不等于征集全部条件通过。

## 十一、部署、许可、安全与五年服务

### 11.1 部署建议

优先确认校级虚拟实验平台能否承载教学门户、用户身份与运行管理。学校统一认证和iLab票据是两种来源身份，应做授权映射；社会用户不能被迫先有浙大学号才能完成开放实验。

教学API部署在受管理服务后，MCTS和仿真任务进入有配额的独立worker队列；为学生显示排队、取消、超时与错误。大模型故障时可保留教师帮助和非AI计算操作，并真实记录AI不可用，不把缓存对话伪装为实时调用。实时MCTS与文献观测重放在界面上区分，教学重放不得冒充当次新搜索。

首版并发承诺应先测再填。以“在线浏览人数”代替“同时运行搜索人数”会误导；分别测门户、AI、MCTS与仿真容量。若一个搜索平均占用t秒、worker数w，理想上界约为3600w/t次每小时，实际还受内存、模型加载、排队和网络影响；本文不据历史单次耗时承诺课堂容量。

### 11.2 资产权利是实质门槛

当前123项来源登记未清理再分发权限，五项模型/模板资产标记redistribute=false。它们不自动禁止任何本地研究用途，也不自动授权公开教学托管；应逐项核验托管、学生访问、展示、修改与分发。原创代码Apache-2.0与原创文档CC BY4.0不能覆盖SciFinder、论文图谱、第三方模型或数据。

征集要求的软件授权范围以及学校软件著作权承诺，应由学校核实；单有Git仓库或开源许可证不等于学校已取得申报所需权利。申报书允许著作权申请中的项目填写受理流水号，但能否符合校内进度仍需办理。

建议建立公开教学准入清单：权利人、许可文本、允许动作、展示范围、五年服务依据、责任人与到期处理。未清楚的材料保留内部，不随课程导出。若现有模型许可无法及时清理，应改用已授权模型/服务和公开可用教学子集，并如实调整功能；不能宣称换个API外壳就解决许可。

### 11.3 安全与持续责任

最低工程事项包括身份校验、会话和数据隔离、教师权限、凭据管理、输入限制、上传与导出权限、审计、备份恢复、依赖维护、个人信息最小化及AI内容越界控制。具体依学校网络安全部门与第三方测评要求落实，本文不是法律合规认证。

等保材料应与实际部署系统匹配。接入已测评平台是否涵盖新AI服务、worker、数据和外部接口，不能默认；取得备案/测评结论及隶属关系证明后再作申报声明。

## 十三、验证设计：需要证明什么

### 13.1 科学内容与仿真

教师核对结构、酶/宿主、反应方向、对照、单位、分析身份及模型域；检查零/缺失/失败保留。对D2/D3使用独立条件检验误差，按教学可辨别的量级事先确定容差；本轮不虚设统一误差阈值。验证范围内可重放、范围外拒绝，未知峰不自动当目标产物。

### 13.2 AI与评分

建立小而有代表性的挑战集：错误糖位点、供体遗漏、加糖/水解混淆、无来源引用、单位错误、超范围酶/底盘组合。验收核心是关键化学错误不被AI默认为真，数值输出来自工具，来源可查，最终分数可复算。具体样本数和通过标准在案例冻结后确定。

记录模型、提示、知识库及工具版本；模型升级后重新核验挑战集。开放题教师最终裁定；对基础不同的学生检查提示可获得性与评分一致性。

### 13.3 教学成效

先用真实小规模试用发现流程问题，再依据课程组织前测/后测或合理对照，评价结构判断、设计、数据解释及证据识别。样本量和统计方案须按实际授课情况制定；不能用接口10条运行记录估计学习增益，不能用满意度代替能力提升。

可以参考虚拟生技实验教育研究设计，但不把其他平台报告的学习效果数字转用为本项目结果。[Bonde等原始教育研究](https://www.nature.com/articles/nbt.2955)

### 13.4 工程与共享

执行身份隔离、越权拒绝、断网/超时恢复、队列、重复上传、完成冻结、两浏览器、带宽提示与备份恢复。明确各项实测时间、软件版本和证据；没有运行的指标记未测/null，不写0失败。

项目拟面向化学及相关专业高年级本科生，以健康相关黄酮糖苷的酶法合成和生物制造为真实问题载体，建设综合设计与研究探索相结合的虚拟实验。依托FlavoRetro已有的结构分析、模型辅助逆合成搜索和反应证据追溯基础，学生先独立设计方案，再审查AI建议，通过对照设置、投料计算、虚拟取样与定量分析比较不同路线，并结合有依据的底盘工程数据解释供体供给、竞争代谢和产物积累问题。

### 3.2 需要优先补建的能力

第一层缺口是“实验”。目前没有学生实验状态机、虚拟投料/取样/分析操作、经过审定的前向反馈模型、独立教学答案和评分。只在搜索框旁添加聊天窗口，仍然不能完成这层转换。

第二层缺口是“教学运行”。当前web.py使用全局BoundedSemaphore(1)，搜索同步执行，忙时返回429；没有学生、班级、教师角色与逐用户运行权限。运行历史按工作区公开，/api/status返回内部STATE和服务器路径。教学门户应与研究管理界面建立权限边界，敏感状态和全工作区历史不应对公共访问者开放。现有前端提交参数也未带领域库开关/版本，不能把后端拥有糖苷模块写成已向学生开放。

第三层缺口是“可持续公开服务”。排队、任务隔离、超时、资源配额、备份、浏览器与网络验证、学校安全证明和外部平台回传都要补齐。父服务与worker的旧领域版本接线还存在静态一致性疑点，须在后续授权建设中回归；本轮未复现，不作为已确认运行缺陷。

### 3.3 科学状态如何影响申报

STATE明确：方法与有限开发交付已完成，正式C/SS独立迁移未验证，TASK-017相关科研准入未通过，科学效果保持null；历史停止与曝光记录保留。

这不等于“不能开展教学建设”。教学版可以限定在教师审定、来源与适用范围清楚的案例，检验学生能否正确设计和分析实验；它不必先证明一个通用逆合成方法对所有黄酮泛化。但应建立独立的教学案例审核与教学验收，不能修改研究门槛或把历史卡片换名变成独立gold。

建议保存三套分开的状态：research_evaluation、teaching_case_review、public_teaching_release。教学公开上线不自动改变前两者；已有科研资产也不自动取得公开教学许可。

## 四、与你的专业及浙大条件的结合

已确认的背景是“浙江大学化学系”和围绕FlavoRetro的黄酮/糖苷结构、反应证据、逆合成软件工作。可以据此设计以下分工，不能进一步推定你的职称、已授课程、论文、实验室资源或产业关系。

化学系应主导目标分子身份、立体与区域选择性、酶法/化学法比较、物料衡算、分析鉴定及证据边界。这些构成项目的学科主体。生物催化或合成生物教师补足酶、宿主、供体代谢、竞争通路和真实实验场景。技术人员负责服务、学习状态、AI适配和iLab；不由软件人员独自裁定酶活与实验答案。

与已有项目背景的融合应体现方法，而不是把全部项目拼接进去：

- FlavoRetro提供结构、路线、搜索与证据追溯。
- 既有条件数据治理经验可帮助设计单位、零/缺失、重复、条件比较与适用范围；CondRxnBench并非现成酶催化预测器，其数据、许可和任务适配不能默认跨项目复用。
- 文献整理经验可支撑教师案例包与来源定位；论文摘要不能直接代替原始定量数据或独立答案。

浙江大学已有虚拟仿真实验共享平台，也公开介绍过合成生物学实验课程。可优先向校内平台确认托管、身份接入、测评适用关系及运行支持，并邀请相应领域教师参与；本文没有联系任何人，也未落实合作。[浙大共享平台](https://ilab.zju.edu.cn/)、[合成生物学课程](https://zjubiolab.zju.edu.cn/page/course/detail/154/2359)

学校AI STEP介绍了虚拟实验建设以及“智海”“浙大先生”等资源，可以作为校内模型服务路线的调研线索，不能假定已有API权限或免费额度。该页面URL含2026，但正文记载的发布事件为2025年3月，本文不把它误写为2026新政策。[浙大AI STEP介绍](https://ai.zju.edu.cn/2026/0112/c89504a3127572/page.htm)

|黄酮糖苷酶法合成设计与有界虚拟实验|高|有条件较强：健康相关天然产物生物制造|中：案例、定量反馈、教学链|首选化学核心|
|同一目标的底盘工程设计与案例验证|中|更直接对应合成生物|中高：专业教师、真实扰动数据、宿主约束|以有限数据模块衔接，完整底盘预测放中期|
|完整细胞工厂/发酵数字孪生|低至中|主题契合|高：时序、传质、代谢、动力学和验证|本轮不承诺|
|AI酶活/底物范围预测与自动优化|结构/证据框架可复用|可服务未来健康|高：可授权训练数据、标签与留组验证|中期独立任务|
|仅逆合成网页加通用AI助教|高|弱且教学实验性不足|低|只能作底层组件|

这里的“高/中/低”为基于依赖关系的定性工程判断，不是客观评分或录取概率。推荐首选与有限底盘模块的组合，是因为它同时保留化学系的主导能力和未来健康的生物制造对象；不会要求五周内重建一套合成生物预测平台。

具体创新表述应落在可检查的教学行为：学生先独立设计再比较AI；每条建议显示来源与适用范围；学生通过对照与定量识别失败；规则可重放评分；学生区分预测、仿真和观测。不要以“自主研发大模型”或“国内首创”替代这些贡献。

## 六、科学场景：为什么优先论证异槲皮苷

候选主目标为异槲皮苷，即槲皮素-3-O-β-D-葡萄糖苷。它与不同位点的槲皮素糖苷、芦丁、酶改性异槲皮苷EMIQ应严格区分，不可仅按名称合并。

外部原始研究提供三个互相关联、又必须分开的教学场景：

|场景|原始研究能支持的内容|模型与教学边界|
|---|---|---|
|槲皮素酶促加糖与供体再生|Pei等2019研究UGT与蔗糖合酶耦合制备异槲皮苷|本轮核到公开摘要，完整条件/原始数据仍需取得与核对|
|芦丁选择性去鼠李糖|Zhang等2015研究重组α-L-rhamnosidase转化，含动力学线索|这是水解，不是UGT糖基化；参数不跨酶/体系迁移|
|工程菌将外加槲皮素转化为产物|Niu等2024研究B.subtilis糖供体、底物降解和产物水解工程|不是从葡萄糖全合成，也不是本校已验证生产工艺|

[Pei等2019](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10600-019-02712-9)、[Zhang等2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25724715/)、[Niu等2024](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12934-024-02390-5)

它们共享目标，适合教授“同一产物可以有不同制造路径”；不能据此共享同一响应面、动力学参数或真值。Niu研究中的供体工程并未单独解决产物积累问题，适合训练学生考察竞争代谢与降解；不要设计“每改一个基因产量就增加固定比例”的游戏规则。

酶候选排序可以作为后续AI方向。Yang等2018的活性预测研究与2025年的GT高通量谱说明该问题有实验数据基础；后者初筛与选定纯酶复核存在差异，数据也不适合直接比较不同底物的催化效率。它们支持“AI建议需要实验核对”，不支持把大规模筛查结果直接转为高可信产率模拟器或全部位点真值。[Yang等2018](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41589-018-0154-9)、[GT高通量原始研究2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-61530-6)

健康关联应表述为“健康相关天然产物研究与制造场景”。合成路线、体外性质、工艺产率不推出临床疗效、给药建议、食品可用性或药品上市资格。教学不需要承担临床决策任务。

## 七、把科研工具变成一次完整虚拟实验

### 7.1 教学对象与学习目标

建议优先面向已学有机化学、分析化学与基础生物化学的高年级本科生，依托综合化学实验、化学生物学或相关课程中的一个实验单元。具体课程名称、学分、教学计划与授课资格须由化学系确定，本文不虚构已纳入课程。

建议4学时，暂按每学时45分钟共180分钟设计，按学校安排调整。完成后应能：

- 正确识别母核、连接位点、糖型及反应方向，区分加糖与去糖。
- 比较自主方案与AI建议，指出证据、范围和缺口。
- 设计对照、投料、取样和定量方案，完成物料衡算。
- 基于观测解释供体、降解与选择性问题，并提出一次有依据的修正。
- 识别模型不可支持的条件，不把AI排序当作成功概率。

这五项是拟实现的学习目标，不是已测到的能力提升。

### 7.2 24步实质性交互方案

每步均要求学生提交选择、数值或理由并获得反馈。登录、加载、浏览下一页、纯视频观看不计步数；实际教学脚本还需教师审定。

|步骤|学生动作|可观察反馈或产物|
|---|---|---|
|01|从结构中确认目标产物并标注糖连接位点|结构与位点校验|
|02|区分芦丁、异槲皮苷和位置异构糖苷|身份差异及错误解释|
|03|判断两条候选反应属于加糖还是去糖|反应方向与键变化|
|04|给来源卡分级，选出能够支持本案例的证据|证据等级与缺口|
|05|独立选择初始路线并提交理由|保存未经AI提示的方案|
|06|登记可检验假设和预期失败原因|假设与观测变量匹配检查|
|07|调用AI/搜索获取限定候选并进行排序|真实调用结果及来源|
|08|拒绝一条超范围建议并说明依据|守卫、证据和拒绝理由反馈|
|09|选择经过审定的酶/反应体系|身份、底物范围和限制|
|10|选择糖供体与再生方案，或解释水解无需该供体|路径特异的物料约束|
|11|设置空白、无酶或对应阴性对照|对照能否识别替代解释|
|12|输入底物、体积与单位并计算投料|单位、摩尔量与守恒检查|
|13|选择数据支持的缓冲/溶剂与pH条件|范围支持或明确拒绝|
|14|选择已测/已标定的温度和酶量档位|适用域及资源消耗|
|15|设计单变量比较，保留基线条件|可比性与混杂检查|
|16|设置取样时点并确认定量方案|采样计划合理性反馈|
|17|执行基线虚拟实验，观察对照和实验组|有来源标签的实验结果|
|18|辨认目标、底物和未知峰，选择积分区间|分析身份/积分错误反馈|
|19|依据标准曲线、稀释倍数计算浓度|可重放的数值检查|
|20|计算转化率、产物收率和选择性并检查衡算|底物消失是否等于产物生成|
|21|为底盘模块选定有证据的宿主与工程方案|显示方案适用性及可用对照|
|22|比较对应工程菌数据，判断供体/降解限制|真实数据差异与未支持解释|
|23|在预算内修改一次方案并运行有支持的比较|第一次与修正结果并列|
|24|提交证据约束的结论、未解问题及下一实验设计|量规反馈与教师复核入口|

模块A为步骤01—20的主实验；模块B为21—22的最低衔接，并在23—24体现方案迭代。若没有可用底盘数据，21—22不能用宣传图替代，应调整教学脚本并重新审核方向契合及实质步数。模块A中的去糖路线可先作为路线对照，不必同时建设两套完整连续动力学模拟器。

学生选择未测的底盘组合时，可保存为研究假设，系统返回“无对应实验数据，不能给定量结果”，并引导设计验证；不能补造预测值来保持流程流畅。

### 7.3 四学时安排与赋分

|学时|主要任务|过程与结果分值|
|---|---|---|
|1|结构、身份、证据，步骤01—06|结构与证据20分|
|2|AI比较、酶/供体、对照及投料，步骤07—12|路线与理由20分|
|3|条件、采样、执行及定量，步骤13—20|实验设计20分、计算分析20分|
|4|底盘比较、一次迭代、解释与独立小测，步骤21—24|迭代与边界20分|

数值题依据固定公式、单位与版本化容差评分；开放题按明确量规，由教师定稿。AI可提供反馈草稿，不单独决定最终成绩。记录提示使用次数用于分析学习过程，不简单按“少用AI=高分”惩罚基础不同的学生。提供统一提示权限、申诉及教师复核，检验不同学习基础群体的评分公平性。

能力画像只记录有证据的结构判断、证据审查、设计、定量、反思五个维度及变化，不能据有限行为贴心理或天赋标签。最优产率不是唯一正确答案；合理识别模型不足也应得分。

## 八、真实实验数据与前向仿真的可行路径

### 8.1 目前“待定”的三个层面

外部论文确实包含真实实验；尚未确定本项目可使用哪些原始/授权数据；本校的课程、实验场景归属、合作教师及补充测定还未落实。这三个层面不同，不能笼统写“没有任何真实数据”，也不能把外部论文变成本校成果。

优先顺序建议：有授权的校内/合作实验数据；可合法教学复用的开放原始数据；经授权和核对的文献图表数字化。摘要终点产率和自行画出的曲线不能支撑定量实验仿真。数字化图数据应标注提取方法和误差，保留原位置，并由教师审核其教学用途。

### 8.2 教学数据包最低内容

每个案例需独立登记目标与底物完整结构、反应方向、酶/宿主身份、糖供体及条件域；投料、体积、单位、取样时点、对照与重复；标准品与标准曲线、色谱或其他可复核分析记录；失败、零、缺失和未知峰；原始数据位置、授权、版本与审核人。

教师审定记录必须显示实际审核者与日期。Cano整理和机器核验只能标agent_delegated，不能预填human_reviewed。原有受限反应库和资料包不整体公开，只使用逐项已准入的教学子集。

### 8.3 仿真按证据选择，不能先承诺连续预测

|等级|实现方式|适用条件|允许输出|
|---|---|---|---|
|D1|真实实验条件的离散查询/重放|有对应条件与可复核数据|明确标记“来源实验数据”|
|D2|有界插值或经验模型|覆盖网格、独立验证和误差足够|标明插值/估计及支持区间|
|D3|经标定机理模型|有足够初速、时序、重复和独立条件|模型预测、参数来源和误差|
|D4|概念演示|无足够定量依据|仅机制示意，不作为定量实验结果或成绩真值|

最现实的申报版以D1为基础，D2/D3在数据允许时增加；离散查询也必须反映真实科学规律，支持学生控制、对照、取样与分析，不能退化成固定答案播放。其能否达到征集“真仿真”要求应由校内学术审核，单有二十次点击不构成达标。

纯酶水解可从单底物Michaelis–Menten起步：dS/dt = −Vmax·S/(Km+S)，但Vmax、酶量、单位、底物范围和失活必须与该酶、体系匹配。不能仅凭论文一个终点唯一确定模型。UGT与供体再生体系应分别处理双底物、UDP与供体循环；没有参数时使用已测离散条件。

底盘模块初期优先使用已有工程组合的真实对照数据；不把基因改动线性叠加。不建设未经验证的连续生长、发酵、传质模型，也不在缺数据时声称数字孪生。所有范围外输入均返回“不支持定量预测”，保存学生假设并提示后续验证。

## 九、AI方向转换与接口架构

### 9.1 四种职责分开

|层次|职责|建议近期实现|验证方法|
|---|---|---|---|
|化学工具/搜索|结构校验、候选路线、证据和范围|复用受控现有模块，教学案例版本冻结|案例合同及结构/范围核验|
|仿真/数据服务|给出受条件控制的实验观测|D1优先，D2/D3有依据才用|守恒、单位、对照、重放与误差|
|大模型导师|解释、追问、检索和工具编排|基于审定案例的检索增强与工具调用|引文存在、越界拒绝、错误挑战集|
|学习/评价服务|状态、步骤、成绩、反馈及iLab|确定性计算与教师量规|重放一致、权限隔离、回传核对|

推荐数据流为“学习者门户 → 教学会话/权限 → AI导师及受控工具 → 仿真与案例数据 → 评分/档案 → iLab适配器”。研究管理接口留在内部，教学运行使用单独命名空间和存储权限。

### 9.2 “AI接口”具体应做什么

模型调用应由后端统一代理，支持校内服务或学校批准的外部服务；模型名称、版本、部署类型、证据快照和提示模板版本记录到会话。不把服务密钥写进网页或学生端。

适合首版的工具包括validate_structure、retrieve_case_evidence、search_candidate_routes、check_experiment_design、run_supported_simulation、calculate_material_balance。它们是拟议内部能力名，不是平台已经提供的API。工具仅接受结构化、经过校验的参数，不提供任意shell、文件读写或访问研究库权限。

导师在实验前帮助发现缺对照和证据；实验中检查单位与异常，提醒“底物下降不等于目标增加”；实验后引导比较假设与观测。结果引用对应case_id、dataset_hash和实验条件。没有证据时明确未知，不补引文、酶活、产率或谱图。

对学生不必展示所有哈希和实现字段，保留可点击的来源、模型/数据类型、适用范围和限制；完整技术指纹供教师和审核使用。

### 9.3 拟议内部教学API

以下为设计建议，尚未实现，路径与字段可在后续任务中细化：

|接口|用途|关键约束|
|---|---|---|
|POST /teaching/sessions|创建经授权的实验会话|用户、课程、案例版本绑定|
|POST /teaching/sessions/{id}/steps|记录学生动作|序号、时间、参数、理由、重复次数|
|POST /teaching/ai/assist|导师提示与证据检索|权限/配额、工具白名单、使用统计|
|POST /teaching/simulations|提交支持域内实验|案例数据域验证；异步返回job_id|
|GET /teaching/jobs/{id}|获取结果与排队状态|只允许所有者或授权教师访问|
|POST /teaching/sessions/{id}/finalize|冻结报告与最终分数|教师量规版本、完整步骤与审计|
|内部iLab上传作业|回传结果/AI统计/报告|服务端凭据、重试与完成冻结|

优先复用研究服务作为内部工具，不让大模型自由指定模型资产或任意版本。教学案例固定领域库与配置，避免普通学生选到未验收的历史版本。

### 9.4 中期AI研究可以如何增长

首版不自训基础大模型。等教学案例积累后，可分别申请有界研究任务：酶/底物候选排序、条件优化建议、实验失败诊断。每项都需要可用标签、明确任务和来源分组留出；不能用学生交互或历史曝光数据立即宣称独立泛化。

可把“预测失败与不确定性”设计为学习任务：AI高排名候选未必有实验支持，学生应发现并提出验证。这样复用现有项目的证据优势，而不是用新大模型遮盖旧证据缺口。

## 十、实验空间2026接口：已经核到哪些内容

官方说明明确：2026年沿用2022接口，新增AI应用过程统计ai_data。无需猜一套新标准；也不能只接普通聊天接口就称完成国家平台对接。[2026接口说明](https://shenbao.ilab-x.com/declare/wiki/v2#1-3)、[官方动态正文](https://shenbao.ilab-x.com/js/wiki_v2.js)

接入流程为：用户在实验空间登录并携ticket跳转实验URL；后端以平台appid及secret按规范换取用户信息和access_token；执行并保存实验；向结果接口提交步骤、分数和AI数据；有实验报告时按规定后续上传。

已核实的生产接口包括https://www.ilab-x.com/open/api/v2/token与https://www.ilab-x.com/open/api/v2/data_upload。token请求含ticket、appid、signature；签名按官方规定使用解码ticket与APPID、SECRET计算MD5并转大写，拼URL时再按规范编码。凭据只在服务端处理，敏感query不进入普通访问日志；有效期及刷新依平台返回和最新规范处理。本次没有申请密钥或实际调用这些业务接口。

### 10.1 官方ai_data字段

|字段|必需|规则|
|---|---|---|
|ai_call_count|是|非负整数，记录真实AI调用次数|
|ai_models_used|是|数组；调用为0可空，大于0不得空|
|ai_usage_scenarios|是|数组；调用大于0不得空且元素不得空|
|ai_input_token_count|否|提交时为非负整数|
|ai_output_token_count|否|提交时为非负整数|
|ai_remark|否|字符串|

模型数组每项必有model、version、deployment，provider可选；deployment枚举为公有云服务、私有化部署、混合服务、本地运行。ai_data及模型元素不能添加未定义字段；相关校验失败返回码19。对2026推荐项目完成记录status=1校验，未完成status=2暂不按该条件校验。

校内应确定“调用”的计数口径：至少将实际导师模型请求与已用模型如实记录，内部另存工具、搜索和错误事件；MCTS内部每一步不能未经定义就当一次大模型调用。非语言模型没有token概念时不伪造token，选填字段按实际能观测的数据提交；最终映射需与平台联调确认。

协议允许一次记录AI调用为0，只是表达和容错规则，不等于项目不需要大模型赋能。不能用接口返回成功代替教学质量审查。

### 10.2 实验过程与结果

原有结果包含username、title、status、score、startTime、endTime、timeUsed、appid、originId、steps；每步含序号、名称、起止时间、实际/合理用时、满分/得分、重复次数、评价和赋分模型。时间戳按规范为13位，用时以秒计。科学参数和来源指针优先内部保存，并按ext_data的允许结构扩展；不要放进禁止额外字段的ai_data。

用同一稳定originId关联本次实验。未完成记录按规范更新，完成后不再修改；最终上传前应复核成绩。超时重试须识别重复记录和既有回执，不能每重试一次创建一条新实验；依照实际错误码管理状态和token刷新。

必须先测试环境、再正式密钥与地址联通。正式自查要求至少3个真实用户、10条真实有效的虚拟实验运行记录，结果与用时应有差异。它不是10份湿实验数据，也不证明教学效果。

**两个步数门槛必须分开：接口完成记录仍按不少于10步校验；本次申报设计要求不少于20步实质性交互。** 本方案按24步设计，并应在实测中核查其真实性。平台已联通不等于征集全部条件通过。

## 十一、部署、许可、安全与五年服务

### 11.1 部署建议

优先确认校级虚拟实验平台能否承载教学门户、用户身份与运行管理。学校统一认证和iLab票据是两种来源身份，应做授权映射；社会用户不能被迫先有浙大学号才能完成开放实验。

教学API部署在受管理服务后，MCTS和仿真任务进入有配额的独立worker队列；为学生显示排队、取消、超时与错误。大模型故障时可保留教师帮助和非AI计算操作，并真实记录AI不可用，不把缓存对话伪装为实时调用。实时MCTS与文献观测重放在界面上区分，教学重放不得冒充当次新搜索。

首版并发承诺应先测再填。以“在线浏览人数”代替“同时运行搜索人数”会误导；分别测门户、AI、MCTS与仿真容量。若一个搜索平均占用t秒、worker数w，理想上界约为3600w/t次每小时，实际还受内存、模型加载、排队和网络影响；本文不据历史单次耗时承诺课堂容量。

### 11.2 资产权利是实质门槛

当前123项来源登记未清理再分发权限，五项模型/模板资产标记redistribute=false。它们不自动禁止任何本地研究用途，也不自动授权公开教学托管；应逐项核验托管、学生访问、展示、修改与分发。原创代码Apache-2.0与原创文档CC BY4.0不能覆盖SciFinder、论文图谱、第三方模型或数据。

征集要求的软件授权范围以及学校软件著作权承诺，应由学校核实；单有Git仓库或开源许可证不等于学校已取得申报所需权利。申报书允许著作权申请中的项目填写受理流水号，但能否符合校内进度仍需办理。

建议建立公开教学准入清单：权利人、许可文本、允许动作、展示范围、五年服务依据、责任人与到期处理。未清楚的材料保留内部，不随课程导出。若现有模型许可无法及时清理，应改用已授权模型/服务和公开可用教学子集，并如实调整功能；不能宣称换个API外壳就解决许可。

### 11.3 安全与持续责任

最低工程事项包括身份校验、会话和数据隔离、教师权限、凭据管理、输入限制、上传与导出权限、审计、备份恢复、依赖维护、个人信息最小化及AI内容越界控制。具体依学校网络安全部门与第三方测评要求落实，本文不是法律合规认证。

等保材料应与实际部署系统匹配。接入已测评平台是否涵盖新AI服务、worker、数据和外部接口，不能默认；取得备案/测评结论及隶属关系证明后再作申报声明。

五年计划应明确年度课程更新、数据/模型版本审核、教师答疑、模型服务费和服务器预算、备份演练、漏洞修复及人员交接。第一年完成限定案例并形成实测档案；第二年在授权数据到位后扩展案例；第三至五年按课程使用反馈更新，停止维护的版本有下线和迁移安排。计划不是已经连续运行五年的证明。

## 十二、资源、工期与2026年申报路线

### 12.1 最小组织方式

建议主要团队围绕负责人/课程教师、化学案例教师、生物催化或底盘教师、平台技术、AI/教学评价统筹，控制在申报表人数范围内；支持开发、测试和校级运维可以另按学校规定提供。本报告不填任何未同意加入的姓名，不把Cano作为实际申报教师。

需要一个有真实责任的课程负责人和一个能审核生物内容的人；仅个人加AI，难以同时关闭科学、教学、上线、许可、等保、试教与材料。

### 12.2 工作量情景估算

以下为内部工作量估算，不是供应商报价、采购预算或交付保证；假定现有底层可复用，且校内平台提供部分承载与安全支持。

|工作包|预计人日|关键依赖|
|---|---|---|
|课程脚本、案例审核与授权数据整理|10—16|课程负责人、真实场景和数据|
|24步实验、分析操作与有界反馈|16—24|审定数据、前端及仿真工程|
|AI导师、工具与证据服务|8—12|批准的模型服务、案例知识|
|会话、评分、队列及权限|12—18|平台与数据库支持|
|iLab映射、统计与联调|6—10|账号、appid/密钥、测试窗口|
|浏览器/容量/教学试用/修复|10—16|可运行完整链与真实使用者|
|视频、材料、运维交接|8—14|定版系统、审查与学校证明|
|合计|70—110|不含无法估期的独立等保和新湿实验等待|

按3名持续投入工程/测试人员每周5个工作日估算，5周约75人日，4名约100人日；专业教师和审批配合仍不可缺。因此只有范围足够小、数据和校级平台很快落实时，五周才有条件接近这一工作量。正常稳健公开版本宜预留8—12周。

经费应采用“人日×学校核定单价 + 托管/模型调用 + 数据/必要补测 + 安全证明 + 视频/运维”的项目化预算。模型费用按真实会话数、调用数及计费token/服务合同核算；本轮未核供应商报价，不提供看似精确的总价。五年运行费用不能只报一次开发费。

### 12.3 按国家节点制定的条件性排程

以下为情景计划，校内截止一经取得即覆盖本表，不能按本表延迟校内报送。

|建议窗口|目标|必须得到的实物|
|---|---|---|
|10-15至10-17|资格、方向、平台和数据决策|校内流程/截止、课程负责人、平台承载意见、案例来源清单|
|10-18至10-23|冻结最小教学合同|审定案例包、24步脚本、评分、数据域、AI及许可清单|
|10-24至11-03|完成可演示主实验和AI服务|端到端学生会话、真实反馈、教师视图、权限与排队|

10月的校内遴选可能早于可运行原型，必须马上向校内负责人确认如何呈现充分前期建设基础。联系人10月12日节点已过，只能核实学校已有安排，不应自行补交或推断失格。

### 12.4 继续、降范围与停止门

|门|继续条件|不满足时|
|---|---|---|
|G0 校内资格与时间|学校流程、推荐资格、课程归属和真实负责人明确|停止宣称本轮申报可执行，保留建设方案|
|G1 真实场景与数据|至少一个完整主案例，生物制造衔接有可审定资料|换有证据案例；不得靠AI补数据|
|G2 教学与仿真|20以上实质步、对照/分析/反馈/评分完整|收缩功能，重新审核实验性；不能用点击凑数|

## 十三、验证设计：需要证明什么

### 13.1 科学内容与仿真

教师核对结构、酶/宿主、反应方向、对照、单位、分析身份及模型域；检查零/缺失/失败保留。对D2/D3使用独立条件检验误差，按教学可辨别的量级事先确定容差；本轮不虚设统一误差阈值。验证范围内可重放、范围外拒绝，未知峰不自动当目标产物。

### 13.2 AI与评分

建立小而有代表性的挑战集：错误糖位点、供体遗漏、加糖/水解混淆、无来源引用、单位错误、超范围酶/底盘组合。验收核心是关键化学错误不被AI默认为真，数值输出来自工具，来源可查，最终分数可复算。具体样本数和通过标准在案例冻结后确定。

记录模型、提示、知识库及工具版本；模型升级后重新核验挑战集。开放题教师最终裁定；对基础不同的学生检查提示可获得性与评分一致性。

### 13.3 教学成效

先用真实小规模试用发现流程问题，再依据课程组织前测/后测或合理对照，评价结构判断、设计、数据解释及证据识别。样本量和统计方案须按实际授课情况制定；不能用接口10条运行记录估计学习增益，不能用满意度代替能力提升。

可以参考虚拟生技实验教育研究设计，但不把其他平台报告的学习效果数字转用为本项目结果。[Bonde等原始教育研究](https://www.nature.com/articles/nbt.2955)

### 13.4 工程与共享

执行身份隔离、越权拒绝、断网/超时恢复、队列、重复上传、完成冻结、两浏览器、带宽提示与备份恢复。明确各项实测时间、软件版本和证据；没有运行的指标记未测/null，不写0失败。

|前期基础|已有黄酮/糖苷研究工作台、真实搜索、证据追溯与研究工程验收|已有成熟虚拟实验或显著教学成效|
|AI能力|已有模型辅助搜索；拟接大模型导师与受控工具|自主训练化学大模型、精准预测酶活/药效|

### 14.2 建设中版本简介草稿

项目拟面向化学及相关专业高年级本科生，以健康相关黄酮糖苷的酶法合成和生物制造为真实问题载体，建设综合设计与研究探索相结合的虚拟实验。依托FlavoRetro已有的结构分析、模型辅助逆合成搜索和反应证据追溯基础，学生先独立设计方案，再审查AI建议，通过对照设置、投料计算、虚拟取样与定量分析比较不同路线，并结合有依据的底盘工程数据解释供体供给、竞争代谢和产物积累问题。

拟建设的大模型导师将贯穿方案设计、实验反馈和反思改进；数值结果由经过审定的实验数据及适用范围明确的模型提供，学习评价采用过程记录、可复算计算及教师量规。项目计划接入学校支持的教学服务和实验空间，形成可共享、可追溯、可持续迭代的实验教学单元。课程、案例数据授权、合作教师、平台承载和安全证明正在落实，教学成效须经实际运行后评价。

这是建设描述草稿，不能直接替代正式申报书，也不能删除“拟/待落实”后作为已有成果提交。

### 14.3 证据与材料清单

正式申报前需形成课程与教学计划文件、真实场景说明、教师审定案例和授权、完整实验手册及24步脚本、评分与能力画像说明、AI伦理和公平性措施、实际URL及容量/浏览器报告、iLab回执与真实运行记录、软件权利/许可材料、等保适用证明、政治审查和学术评价、视频、五年建设与经费责任计划。

简介视频3分钟应呈现真实问题、学生操作、AI与仿真分工及已有基础；教学视频5分钟应展示一次真实可运行实验的关键操作、反馈、结果与评分。可以加速录制流程，但不能用剪辑把未实现功能表示成已运行。

## 十五、最终决策建议

**建议继续准备，暂不把当前项目认定为申报就绪。** 将本轮改造目标限定为健康相关黄酮糖苷生物制造教学，先完成可审定主案例与有限底盘衔接；以化学系为主导，补齐生物催化教师和校级平台支持。

未来48小时最有价值的工作是确认校内本轮流程/截止及课程负责人、找到能够归属并授权的真实实验场景、取得校级平台承载及测评适用路径。三项形成明确答案后，再授权一个独立的建设TASK，冻结案例、功能、人员、预算和提交节点。

若三项能迅速关闭且有3—4名持续投入的工程/测试支持，2026年申报存在条件性机会；若仍由个人加AI且数据/安全承载未定，按36天完成全部公开要求的风险很高。此时应把FlavoRetro先建成可信的校级教学原型，并持续积累真实教学证据。

本次已完成的是调研、源码审计、政策/文献核验与方案文档；没有改动项目功能，没有开展模型/MCTS或教学实验，没有恢复停止研究，没有对外联系、部署或上传。建设建议不改变既有研究合同、科学指标或授权边界。

浙江大学化学系｜建设决策稿 v1.0｜2026年10月15日（Asia/Shanghai）

本报告按所有者“完整分析项目并给出可行方向”的要求编制。用户已确认申报学校为浙江大学、单位为化学系；依托课程、具体负责人、真实实验数据授权和合作实验室尚待落实。结论依据当前仓库静态审计、平台官方十月版申报书与征集说明、2026接口正文及目标检索的原始研究。本文的建设方案、工作量与验收目标均为建议，不是已实现功能、已开展教学或获推荐事实。

## 一、核心结论与建议选题

**有条件可行，值得推进，但当前版本不能直接改名上传。** FlavoRetro 已经拥有真实 AI 搜索、黄酮糖苷结构与反应证据、可追溯运行和网页工作台。它最有价值的转换是：把“研究者寻找候选路线”转成“学生提出方案、审查 AI、执行有依据的虚拟实验、分析结果并修正设计”。

主推荐题名：

**AI赋能健康相关黄酮糖苷的酶法合成与生物制造虚拟仿真实验**

推荐归属为“未来健康—合成生物相关实验教学”，具体以健康相关天然产物的制造问题、酶催化与糖供体工程为对象。题名保留化学系的结构、选择性、物料衡算和分析化学优势；不直接承诺完整底盘细胞自动设计、药效预测或发酵数字孪生。

最小建设范围建议为“一个主目标、两类教学模块、一条完整实验闭环”：

- 主目标：优先论证异槲皮苷，最终由化学与生物催化教师审定身份、来源、条件和数据。
- 模块A：围绕酶法合成/选择性转化，比较糖基化、供体再生和去糖路线，完成投料、对照、取样、定量与结果解释。
- 模块B：用同一目标的已报道工程菌案例，让学生选择有证据的底盘与供体/降解通路方案，比较相应真实数据，解释“表达了酶却未高产”的原因。
- AI贯穿实验前、中、后：方案提示与证据检索、过程诊断、实验后反思；数值结果由独立仿真/数据服务给出，评分由规则和教师量规定稿。

**本轮能否申报，首先取决于三件事：校内推荐与课程资格、真实实验场景及案例数据、可承载公开服务并有适用安全证明的平台。** AI接口开发本身并非最难的一项。

若模块B只能做论文浏览，报告与申报中应称“底盘工程案例分析”，不能写成完整“底盘细胞设计”。若仅有纯逆合成和无细胞酶反应，也不能自行认定已充分符合未来健康的合成生物口径，应请校内组织审核方向契合。未来制造中的生物制造可作为方向口径不被认可时的备选，但不能为此随意更换科学内容。

### 3.2 需要优先补建的能力

第一层缺口是“实验”。目前没有学生实验状态机、虚拟投料/取样/分析操作、经过审定的前向反馈模型、独立教学答案和评分。只在搜索框旁添加聊天窗口，仍然不能完成这层转换。

第二层缺口是“教学运行”。当前web.py使用全局BoundedSemaphore(1)，搜索同步执行，忙时返回429；没有学生、班级、教师角色与逐用户运行权限。运行历史按工作区公开，/api/status返回内部STATE和服务器路径。教学门户应与研究管理界面建立权限边界，敏感状态和全工作区历史不应对公共访问者开放。现有前端提交参数也未带领域库开关/版本，不能把后端拥有糖苷模块写成已向学生开放。

第三层缺口是“可持续公开服务”。排队、任务隔离、超时、资源配额、备份、浏览器与网络验证、学校安全证明和外部平台回传都要补齐。父服务与worker的旧领域版本接线还存在静态一致性疑点，须在后续授权建设中回归；本轮未复现，不作为已确认运行缺陷。

## 四、与你的专业及浙大条件的结合

已确认的背景是“浙江大学化学系”和围绕FlavoRetro的黄酮/糖苷结构、反应证据、逆合成软件工作。可以据此设计以下分工，不能进一步推定你的职称、已授课程、论文、实验室资源或产业关系。

化学系应主导目标分子身份、立体与区域选择性、酶法/化学法比较、物料衡算、分析鉴定及证据边界。这些构成项目的学科主体。生物催化或合成生物教师补足酶、宿主、供体代谢、竞争通路和真实实验场景。技术人员负责服务、学习状态、AI适配和iLab；不由软件人员独自裁定酶活与实验答案。

与已有项目背景的融合应体现方法，而不是把全部项目拼接进去：

- FlavoRetro提供结构、路线、搜索与证据追溯。
- 既有条件数据治理经验可帮助设计单位、零/缺失、重复、条件比较与适用范围；CondRxnBench并非现成酶催化预测器，其数据、许可和任务适配不能默认跨项目复用。
- 文献整理经验可支撑教师案例包与来源定位；论文摘要不能直接代替原始定量数据或独立答案。

浙江大学已有虚拟仿真实验共享平台，也公开介绍过合成生物学实验课程。可优先向校内平台确认托管、身份接入、测评适用关系及运行支持，并邀请相应领域教师参与；本文没有联系任何人，也未落实合作。[浙大共享平台](https://ilab.zju.edu.cn/)、[合成生物学课程](https://zjubiolab.zju.edu.cn/page/course/detail/154/2359)

学校AI STEP介绍了虚拟实验建设以及“智海”“浙大先生”等资源，可以作为校内模型服务路线的调研线索，不能假定已有API权限或免费额度。该页面URL含2026，但正文记载的发布事件为2025年3月，本文不把它误写为2026新政策。[浙大AI STEP介绍](https://ai.zju.edu.cn/2026/0112/c89504a3127572/page.htm)
